# The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick free-energy limiting law

Coordinate `EN-115-000-0020-2-2026-PR-T4-UK-EX-M2-C-PH-H-0415` | `PM-217.1` | status ACTIVE | original slug `The-low-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-free-energy-limiting-law-September-24-2026` | date 2026-09-24 | derived from the openai/math preprint The-low-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-free-energy-limiting-law-September-24-2026, modified (Apache-2.0). ```json
{
  "abstract_verbatim": "For every fixed inverse temperature <i>β</i> &gt; 1, we prove that the zero-field Gaussian Ising Sherrington–Kirkpatrick free energy, centered by its expectation and divided by its standard deviation, converges in distribution to a nondegenerate law as the system size tends to infinity through all integers. We also prove that its variance divided by <i>n</i><sup>1/3</sup> converges to a finite positive constant.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> For every fixed inverse temperature <i>β</i> &gt; 1, we prove that the zero-field Gaussian Ising Sherrington–Kirkpatrick free energy, centered by its expectation and divided by its standard deviation, converges in distribution to a nondegenerate law as the system size tends to infinity through all integers. We also prove that its variance divided by <i>n</i><sup>1/3</sup> converges to a finite positive constant.

- **claim-standardized-limiting-law** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): For every fixed real $\beta>1$, there is a nondegenerate Borel probability measure $\nu_\beta$ such that $$X_n(\beta)\ \Longrightarrow\ \nu_\beta \qquad\text{as }n\to\infty\text{ through all integers}.$$ The measure $\nu_\beta$ has mean zero, variance one, and a finite exponential moment in a neighborhood of the origin. It is the unique probability measure with the moments specified in Proposition <a href="#def:law" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:law">3</a> below.
  - Explanation: Exact finite-size standardization yields full-sequence weak convergence to a nondegenerate, moment-determinate law.
- **claim-moment-convergence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-moments)): For each fixed $\beta>1$, there are real numbers $a_k=a_k(\beta)$, $k\ge1$, with the following property. For every integer $k\ge1$, there are constants $c_k>0$ and $C_k<\infty$ such that $$\label{eq:moment-rate} \big\|\mathbb E Y_n^k-a_k\big\|\le C_k n^{-c_k},\qquad n\ge2.$$ There are also constants $c>0$ and $C<\infty$, depending on $\beta$, for which $$\label{eq:exponential-moments} \sup_{n\ge2}\mathbb E e^{c\|Y_n\|}\le C.$$ The limits satisfy $a_1=0$ and $0<a_2<\infty$.
  - Explanation: Completed centered fluctuations have power-rate moment convergence, uniformly controlled exponential tails, and a positive limiting variance.
- **claim-finite-system-moment-specification** (construction, [source](#stmt-def-law)): Fix $\beta>1$ and let $C=\sum_{l=2}^{\infty}l^{-2}$. For an integer $k\ge1$, draw an integer $J\ge2$ with $$\mathbb P(J=l)=\frac{l^{-2}}C.$$ Conditional on $J$, draw $k+1$ independent copies $F_J^{c,0},\ldots,F_J^{c,k}$ of the completed free energy in <a href="#eq:completed-free-energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:completed-free-energy">[eq:completed-free-energy]</a>. Set $$t=\log J, \qquad P_k=\prod_{i=1}^k J^{-1/6}(F_J^{c,0}-F_J^{c,i}).$$ Conditional averaging over the independent comparison copies gives $\mathbb E[P_k\mid J=l]=\mathbb E Y_l^k$. The constants in Theorem <a href="#thm:moments" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:moments">2</a> satisfy $$\label{eq:law-moments} a_k=C\sum_{h=0}^{\infty} \mathbb E\!\left[P_k\left(\frac{t^h}{h!} -\mathbf1_{\{h\ge1\}}\frac{t^{h-1}}{(h-1)!}\right)\right],$$ where the second term is absent for $h=0$. Each expectation is taken before the series is summed. The series of these scalar expectations is absolutely convergent. We have $a_2>0$, and the law in Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a> is uniquely determined by $$\int z^k\,\nu_\beta(dz)=\frac{a_k}{a_2^{k/2}},\qquad k\ge1.$$
  - Explanation: An absolutely convergent series of finite-system expectations determines the limiting moments; the expectations precede summation.
- **claim-curie-weiss-invariance** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cor-skcw)): Fix $\beta>1$ and $0\le\gamma<1$. Using the same independent standard Gaussian couplings as in <a href="#eq:model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:model">[eq:model]</a>, define the exponent and log partition function $$\begin{gathered} \mathcal H_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\sigma;\beta,\gamma) = \frac{\beta}{\sqrt n}\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}g_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j +\frac{\gamma}{2n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^n\sigma_i\right)^2,\\ F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma) =\log\sum_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n} e^{\mathcal H_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\sigma;\beta,\gamma)}. \end{gathered}$$ Here $\gamma$ is the ferromagnetic coupling already in the exponent. As $n\to\infty$ through all integers, $$\begin{gathered} \mathop{\mathrm{Var}}F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma) \sim a_2(\beta)n^{1/3},\\ \frac{F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma) -\mathbb E F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma)} {\sqrt{\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma)}} \Longrightarrow\nu_\beta. \end{gathered}$$ Here $a_2(\beta)>0$ is the constant $a_2$ above at the same $\beta$. The centering and standard deviation are the perturbed model’s own exact finite-size quantities.
  - Explanation: The displayed ferromagnetic perturbation preserves the limiting variance prefactor and standardized law within its fixed coupling regime.
- **claim-annealed-disorder-chaos** (bound, [source](#stmt-cor-disorder-chaos)): Fix $\beta>1$ and $n\ge2$. Put $E_n=\{(i,j):1\le i<j\le n\}$ and $M=\|E_n\|=n(n-1)/2$, and let $g'$ be an independent copy of $g=(g_{ij})_{(i,j)\in E_n}$ in <a href="#eq:model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:model">[eq:model]</a>. Write $\langle\cdot\rangle_{g,h}$ for expectation under the product of that model’s Gibbs laws with disorders $g,h$, and $R=n^{-1}\sum_i\sigma_i\tau_i$ for the overlap. Thus the replicas are independent conditional on their disorders; $\mathbb E$ below also averages the disorder and any replacement set.* *For $t>0$, set $g^t=e^{-t}g+\sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}\,g'$. For an integer $0\le k\le M$, let $A$ be independent of $g,g'$ and uniform over the $k$-element subsets of $E_n$. Set $g^A_{ij}=g'_{ij}$ on $A$ and $g^A_{ij}=g_{ij}$ otherwise. Then $$\begin{aligned} \mathbb E\langle R^2\rangle_{g,g^t} &\le \frac1n+\frac{2\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}F_n(\beta)} {\beta^2n(1-e^{-t})},\label{eq:chaos-ou}\\ \mathbb E\langle R^2\rangle_{g,g^A} &\le \frac1n+\frac{2(M+1)\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}F_n(\beta)} {\beta^2n(k+1)}+C_\beta n^{-1/2},\label{eq:chaos-replacement} \end{aligned}$$ for a finite constant $C_\beta$ depending only on $\beta$. As $n\to\infty$, for $t_n\ge0$ and integers $0\le k_n\le M$, these bounds imply $$\begin{aligned} t_n n^{2/3}\to\infty &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathbb E\langle R^2\rangle_{g,g^{t_n}}\to0,\\ (k_n/M)n^{2/3}\to\infty &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathbb E\langle R^2\rangle_{g,g^{A_n}}\to0, \end{aligned}$$ where $A_n$ has size $k_n$ as above.
  - Explanation: Variance inequalities give sufficient annealed decorrelation scales for Gaussian drift and uniformly sampled coordinate replacements.
- **claim-pressure-source-projection-estimates** (bound, [source](#stmt-found-estimates)): For the positive laws just defined, the following identities and inequalities hold at every fixed size. The moment bounds in <a href="#eq:A1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A1">[eq:A1]</a>–<a href="#eq:A2" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A2">[eq:A2]</a> hold for every fixed real $2\le p<\infty$, with deterministic $k\in L^2(0,a)$ and zero deterministic external field. $$\begin{split} df_m&=-\tfrac14\int B_v\,db(v)\,dv-\tfrac12\int S_v\,dh(v)\,dv,\\ vC_v\preceq H_v\preceq a C_v,\qquad d S_v&\ge m\,\mathbf E\operatorname{tr}H_v^2\,dh,\qquad \mathbf EW_v=\mathbf E\operatorname{tr}C_v H_v,\\ \left\\|\int k_v(L_v-\mathbf EL_v)dv\right\\|_p^2&\le c_p\left\\|\int k_v^2 W_v\,dv\right\\|_{p/2}. \end{split} \tag{A1}\label{eq:A1}$$ The last line is a moment estimate under the full single-path law, with deterministic weights $k_v$ and zero deterministic external field. More generally, for polynomials $P_v$ of fixed degree with bounded deterministic coefficients, $$\left\\|\int k_v(P_v(L_v)-\mathbf E P_v(L_v))dv\right\\|_p^2 \le c_p\left\\|\int k_v^2 P'_v(L_v)^2 W_v\,dv\right\\|_{p/2}. \tag{A2}\label{eq:A2}$$* *For the projection bound only, assume that the total clocks are at most a fixed power of $\log N$, and that the positive mass and field length are bounded below by inverse powers of $N$. If a branch has traversed a pure or mixed clock interval with field length $\Delta h>0$ after separating from the data determining an anchor vector $V$, and its mass is at least $v>0$ throughout that interval, then for every fixed even $p\ge2$, $$\\|V\cdot(y-X_{\rm end})\\|_p \lesssim_p \frac{\log^2 N}{v\sqrt{m\Delta h}}\,\\|V\\|_p \tag{A3}\label{eq:A3}$$* *where the vector norm inside $L^p$ is Euclidean. The branch must retain its normalized future kernel conditional on the prefix and outside data; in particular, the bound applies to conditionally independent resamplings.
  - Explanation: Pressure differentiation, source Hessians, deterministic-weight moments, and normalized-future projection estimates have distinct stated hypotheses.
- **claim-finite-cavity-quotient** (bound, [source](#stmt-found-cavity-quotient)): For overlap-polynomial $P$ invariant as after <a href="#eq:A4" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A4">[eq:A4]</a>, on any fixed finite-label tree including $ij$, one has through order $k-1$ $$\nu[P Q^*_{ij}]=\nu[P(N_{ij,K}/\Psi_K)_{<k}] +{\rm Rem}_k+O(m^{-1}), \tag{A7}\label{eq:A7}$$ where ${\rm Rem}_k$ has at least $k$ insertions $J$, times $P$.
  - Explanation: Removing a site expresses overlap tests through a finite scalar quotient with insertion and contact remainders.
- **claim-scalar-reference-change** (theorem, [source](#stmt-found-reference-change)): Apply <a href="#eq:A7" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A7">[eq:A7]</a> at a monotone reference $K'$, then Taylor-expand its deterministic scalar coefficients from $K$ to $K'$. At any consistent total truncation, the result is the quotient with reference $K$ and combined argument $J=(h+bQ^*-K')+(K'-K)$.
  - Explanation: Consistent finite truncation combines reference changes with the original mismatch in the scalar quotient.
- **claim-formal-row-derivative** (theorem, [source](#stmt-found-row-derivative)): Let a dot vary $b,h,K,q$ at fixed interval length $a$, and let ${\cal D}$ differentiate <a href="#eq:A6" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A6">[eq:A6]</a> including its scalar coefficients, with the formal rule ${\cal D}\Delta=-e\Delta$ for any fixed $e$. Thus ${\cal D}Q^*=\dot q-e\Delta$; this rule acts on the symbolic polynomial and does not differentiate a random spin sample. Up to deterministic terms common to the two ensembles and Taylor remainders, $$\dot f_m^{\,s}\ \equiv\ (\nu[{\cal D}{\cal I}])_\#. \tag{A9}\label{eq:A9}$$ The same formula applies with superscript $s=0$. The error and its differentiated weights are as described in the proof below.
  - Explanation: Differentiating the finite pressure symbol reproduces pressure derivatives after cancellations; the formal overlap rule does not differentiate sampled spins.
- **claim-finite-site-increment** (bound, [source](#stmt-found-size-increment)): At fixed clocks and $s$, assume that $bq^2$ is nondecreasing. For every fixed positive integer $j$, the change from $m\psi_m$ to $(m+j)\psi_{m+j}$, expanded through total order $k$, is a polynomial in $j$ of degree at most $k$ with zero constant term. Its linear coefficient is the difference of the per-root expectations of <a href="#eq:A6" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A6">[eq:A6]</a>, with $\log\Psi$ truncated after degree $k$. The remainder has the total-pressure bounds given below.
  - Explanation: A fixed finite site increment is polynomial to the retained order, with a linear coefficient given by the common pressure symbol.
- **claim-regular-base-profile** (theorem, [source](#stmt-paths-base-profile)): At fixed $T>1$, the scalar minimizing distribution has support $[0,\xi_*]$, satisfies $\Gamma_0(\xi)=\xi/T$ there, and has a positive initial density. Its active-side distribution function has bounded one-sided derivatives of every fixed order. Moreover $p_{\rm top}=A_0(\xi_*-)$ belongs to $(0,1)$.
  - Explanation: The scalar minimizer has interval support, positive initial density, smooth active-side behavior, and a nonempty terminal plateau.
- **claim-quantitative-scalar-lift** (bound, [source](#stmt-paths-lift)): Uniformly (extending by a terminal annealed clock), $$\begin{array}{ll} b_\circ\asymp1,\quad 1-b_\circ\Gamma'(t)\ \ge c\lambda\min(t^2,1) & (t\ge0),\\ 1-b_\circ\Gamma'(t)\ \le C\lambda t^2 & (0\le \xi\le \xi_*;\ \text{active side}),\\ t(v)\asymp v,\quad q(v)\asymp v & \text{near }0,\quad q(v)\asymp v\text{ throughout}. \end{array} \tag{P2}\label{eq:P2}$$
  - Explanation: The perturbed scalar profile creates a positive response gap with quadratic behavior near the origin.
- **claim-reference-parameter-regularity** (bound, [source](#stmt-paths-parameter-regularity)): Let the direct and smoothed scalar references have the parameters in <a href="#eq:P1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:P1">[eq:P1]</a>, with $1\le\ell\le2^{1/6}$; the smoothed reference is at final strength. The following bounds hold uniformly for sufficiently large $N$. Every derivative order and compact time interval is fixed before $N\to\infty$.* *For the direct reference, the normalized inverse near zero has uniformly bounded one-sided derivatives of every fixed order. Their $\log\lambda$ derivatives are $O(\lambda)$, and $$\partial_{\log\lambda}q(v)=O(\lambda\min(v,1)).$$ At fixed sufficiently small normalized time $\xi$, the $\log\lambda$ derivative of $1-\widehat\Gamma'(\xi)/\widehat\Gamma'(0)$ is $O(\lambda\xi^2)$.* *For the smoothed reference, write $\widehat V_j$ and $\widehat\Gamma_j$ to display the terminal mass $j=4/\ell$. On each fixed compact scalar-time interval $[0,R]$, and for every fixed spatial order $r\ge1$, there are constants $C_r,c_r>0$ such that $$\sup_{0\le\xi\le R,\ z\in\mathbb R} \left\|\partial_j\partial_z^r\widehat V_j(\xi,z)\right\| \le C_r e^{-c_rM}.$$ For a fixed sufficiently small $\xi_0>0$, this implies the more precise cancellation $$\left\|\partial_j\bigl( \widehat\Gamma'_j(\xi)-\widehat\Gamma'_j(0)\bigr)\right\| \le C e^{-cM}\xi^2, \qquad 0\le\xi\le\xi_0. \tag{P2a}\label{eq:P2a}$$ For a fixed sufficiently small mass $v_0>0$, the smoothed reference also satisfies, for each fixed $r\ge0$, $$\sup_{0\le v\le v_0} \bigl(\|\partial_v^r t\|+\|\partial_v^r q\| +\|\partial_\theta\partial_v^r t\| +\|\partial_\theta\partial_v^r q\|\bigr)\le C_r,$$ with one-sided derivatives at zero. The physical initial spatial derivatives obey the rescaling bound, for each fixed $r\ge1$, $$\left\|\partial_\theta\left( \ell^{1-r}\partial_z^r V(0,0)\right)\right\| \le C_r e^{-c_rM}.$$* *Over the full mass interval $(0,4)$, the smoothed clocks $t,q$ are absolutely continuous in $\theta$, with $$\int_0^4\bigl(\|\partial_\theta t(v)\| +\|\partial_\theta q(v)\|\bigr)\,dv \le C M^C. \tag{P2b}\label{eq:P2b}$$ The constants in this integrated bound contain no inverse power of $\omega$.
  - Explanation: Strength and size derivatives retain the required local cancellations and have controlled full-mass integrals without inverse smoothing losses.
- **claim-regularization-switch** (bound, [source](#stmt-paths-switch)): At final strength $\lambda=x^{p_*}$, with $(\chi_{\rm lin},\chi_e)=(1,0)$, the direct and smoothed systems satisfy <a href="#eq:P11" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:P11">[eq:P11]</a>, uniformly with the same parameters $\gamma,\ell$. Their scalar trial gaps $$f_{\rm spin}(K)+\frac14\int b^{-1}(K-h)^2\,dv-f_m^0,$$ where $f_{\rm spin}$ is the self-corrected one-site pressure at the corresponding terminal mass, also differ by $O(x^{5+c})$. The same fixed $c>0$ works for these three comparisons, independently of the site count.
  - Explanation: Direct and smoothed regularizations agree to a strict power saving for the pressure comparisons and scalar trial gaps.
- **claim-stopped-pressure-increments** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-increment)): There is a choice of the exponents in <a href="#eq:P1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:P1">[eq:P1]</a> and a constant $c>0$ with the following property. For every sufficiently small fixed $\varepsilon>0$, every fixed $q>0$, and $s=q x^{1+\varepsilon}$, the following bounds hold for every sufficiently large fixed stencil order:* 1. *On each direct segment, $$\int \mathbf E_\gamma\!\left[ {\bf1}_{\{\mathcal K_m(s)\le3x^\varepsilon\}} \|\dot\psi_m(s)\|\right]\,\|d\vartheta\| \lesssim x^{5+c},$$ uniformly for $N/2\le m\le3N$, where $\vartheta$ is that segment’s parameter.* 2. *On the size segment the corresponding bound holds for $$\left\|\dot\psi_m(s)+\sum_{j=0}^r c_j(m+j)\psi_{m+j}(s)\right\|.\tag{I}\label{eq:I}$$ It also holds when $m$ is a measurable function of $\theta$ with values in this integer range, or when the observables are averaged with nonnegative probability weights on these integers depending measurably on $\theta$.* *All integrations use absolute path-parameter length. The saving $c$ can be chosen independently of sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. Constants may depend on the fixed test coefficient $q$, stencil order, and the fixed temperature.
  - Explanation: Stopped direct derivatives and combined size increments have summable power savings, also under measurable averaging over site counts.
- **claim-exponential-augmentation** (bound, [source](#stmt-red-lem-augmentation)): Let $G_m$ be the continuation in <a href="#eq:A4" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A4">[eq:A4]</a>, and let $\mathcal E_{x/2}$ be an independent exponential random variable of rate $x/2$. Along every physical path used above, $G_m+\mathcal E_{x/2}$ has a log-concave density. On $\mathcal K_m(s)\le3x^\varepsilon$, the Radon–Nikodym density $$R_m=\frac{e^{sG_m}}{\mathbf E e^{sG_m}}$$ has bounded $L^p$ norm for every fixed finite $p$, uniformly in the path and the allowed site counts for all sufficiently large $N$.
  - Explanation: Exponential augmentation gives log-concavity, allowing the stopped Laplace bound to control all required fixed density moments.
- **claim-site-smoothing-errors** (bound, [source](#stmt-red-lem-site-smoothing)): For any sequence $Z_m$, supported or restricted to the relevant neighborhood of the center, $$\frac{d}{dn}\sum_m w_m(n)Z_m =\sum_m w_m(n)\sum_{j=0}^r c_j Z_{m+j} +O_r\!\left(D^{-r-1}\sup_m\|Z_m\|\right).$$ At the same clock data, uniformly along the paths under consideration, $$\label{red:eq-neighbor} \|\mathcal K_{m+1}(s)-\mathcal K_m(s)\|\le Cs(1+M).$$
  - Explanation: Smooth site weights convert a real derivative into a finite stencil, while neighboring transforms remain uniformly close.
- **claim-dyadic-transform-comparison** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-red-prop-dyadic)): Assume Proposition <a href="#prop:increment" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:increment">15</a>. There is $c'>0$, independent of sufficiently small fixed $\varepsilon$, such that for every fixed positive test coefficient $q$, every integer $N'\in[N,2N]$, and $s=q x^{1+\varepsilon}$, $$\left\|\log\mathbb E e^{(s/x)Y_{N'}} -\log\mathbb E e^{(s/x)Y_N}\right\| \lesssim x^{\varepsilon+c'},\qquad Y_m=m^{-1/6}(F_m^c-\mathbb EF_m^c).$$ The constants are uniform in the integer $N'$.
  - Explanation: The increment estimate controls centered transforms uniformly across every integer endpoint in a dyad.
- **claim-full-sequence-moment-deduction** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-red-prop-moments)): Assume Proposition <a href="#prop:increment" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:increment">15</a>. For every fixed integer $k\ge1$, the moments $\mathbb EY_n^k$ converge at a positive power rate. Their limiting second moment is finite and strictly positive, and the centered variables $Y_n$ have uniformly bounded exponential moments on some constant neighborhood of the origin. They converge weakly to a moment-determinate law. Removing the completion and standardizing by the exact finite-size variance gives the convergence asserted in Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>.
  - Explanation: Dyadic transform comparisons yield power-rate moments, positive variance, exponential integrability, and exact-standardized weak convergence.
- **claim-law-specification-validity** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-red-prop-identification)): Under Proposition <a href="#prop:increment" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:increment">15</a>, the constants in Proposition <a href="#def:law" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:law">3</a> are well defined by an absolutely convergent series after the indicated expectations. They are precisely the limiting centered moments of $Y_n$, with $a_2>0$. The standardized moments $a_k/a_2^{k/2}$ determine one Borel probability measure uniquely. Each $a_k$ is also the expectation of a single integrable random variable constructed from fixed priors and finitely many Gaussian systems almost surely.
  - Explanation: The finite-system series gives precisely the limiting moments and admits an integrable unbiased representation using almost surely finite experiments.
- **claim-pair-kernel-inverse** (bound, [source](#stmt-inv-pair-inverse)): The kernel <a href="#eq:A8" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A8">[eq:A8]</a> is considered on extensions of any *fixed* finite list of old labels. A pair function $u_{ab}$ may depend on the topology with those labels but ignores any unused extra labels (is pulled back by restriction). Indices in this section used as pair arguments are distinct leaves. Normalize terminal mass to 1; other bounded terminal masses reduce to this by mass rescaling, scaling cumulative covariances by the square of the mass. Take a monotone step scalar path $K$, nonnegative bounded-variation step multiplier $b$, and retain pair levels in a terminal interval of the hierarchy (the whole interval is allowed). Suppose at these levels $$1-b_r\mathbf E\chi_r^2\ge e>0,\qquad \chi_r=V_{zz}(K_r,Z_{K_r}).$$ Bounds called polynomial in this section are in $1+K_{\rm top}+\\|b\\|_\infty+\operatorname{var}b+e^{-1}$, independent of the number of steps. On the retained levels $$u_{ab}\ \longmapsto\ u_{ab}-\sum_{cd\ {\rm retained}}{\bf M}_{ab,cd} b_{cd}u_{cd} \tag{H1}\label{eq:H1}$$ has an inverse on each finite step resolution. Each output is an integral of inputs over allocations of up to two more labels (some arguments can also be reused), with weights dominated by a polynomial times the ordinary *absolute* unrestricted attachment rules to the old tree including $ab$. Restrictions and bounded weights can depend on the topology. This formulation in particular controls new split densities, allowing coincidences and ties to existing forks. It applies with $ab$ using old labels too. We only need symmetric arrays (on antisymmetric ones the subtracted sum is zero).
  - Explanation: A strict scalar gap permits finite-resolution inversion with polynomial absolute attachment domination uniform in hierarchy refinement.
- **claim-sector-response** (bound, [source](#stmt-inv-sector-response)): Use the finite resolution above, and put $m_t=V_z(K_t,Z_{K_t})$, $\chi_t=V_{zz}(K_t,Z_{K_t})$. Let $\mathbf E_t$ condition on the scalar prefix through $K_t$. On the row-zero sector, different sheets do not mix. On sheet $r$, the multiplier in the child resolutions $\widetilde E_i^r\otimes\widetilde E_l^r$, $i,l\ge r+1$, is $$g_r^{il}=\mathbf E[(\mathbf E_r\chi_{i-1}) (\mathbf E_r\chi_{l-1})].$$ On the additive sector associated with $E_k$, the action on sheet coefficients is $$({\bf M}^k f)_r=g_r^k f_r-\sum_t B^k_{rt}\mu_t^k f_t,\qquad g_t^k=\mathbf E[\chi_t\chi_{\max(k-1,t)}]. \tag{H2}\label{eq:H2}$$ Here $A=K_{k-1}$, with $A=0$ for $k=0$, and $$B^k_{rt}=\mathbf E\left[ \operatorname{Hess}_{z,\alpha}V(A,Z_A)[\beta_r,\beta_t]\right], \qquad \beta_t=\begin{cases} (m_t,0),&t<k,\\ (0,\delta_{K_t}),&t\ge k. \end{cases}$$ The Hessian varies the starting field and the subsequent mass profile. The prefix values $m_t$, $t<k$, are held fixed during this differentiation, and $\delta_{K_t}$ denotes an impulse in the subsequent profile. Expectation is taken after evaluating the Hessian. The matrix $B^k$ is positive semidefinite. Restricting either action to retained levels discards the other input and output sheets.* *The kernels $B^k,g^k$ are bounded and Lipschitz in their evaluation times with polynomial constants. Their changes with the resolution index satisfy $$\\|B^{k+1}-B^k\\|_\infty+\\|g^{k+1}-g^k\\|_\infty \lesssim_{\rm pol}p_k(K_k-K_{k-1}).$$ A successive difference of $g_r^{il}$ in index $i$ is bounded by $Cp_i(K_i-K_{i-1})$; a mixed difference is bounded by the product of the corresponding two bounds. Moreover $0\le g_r^k,g_r^{il}\le\mathbf E\chi_r^2$. These formulas apply with arbitrary old-label topologies under the coefficient convention just described. For $k=0$, their Hessian kernel also satisfies $$\|B^0_{rt}\|\lesssim C(1+K_{R+1})^C K_{\min(r,t)}$$ when the earlier evaluation time is small.
  - Explanation: Row-zero and additive sectors have explicit scalar actions; positivity and weighted differences support the inverse construction.
- **claim-global-unseeded-trial-gap** (bound, [source](#stmt-global-trial-gap)): For the direct paths, use the matrix $b$ of <a href="#eq:P3" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:P3">[eq:P3]</a> and the *unmasked, unseeded* field $h_*=t-bq$ in the untilted system. Fix $T>1$ and the exponent choices of Section <a href="#sec:paths" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:paths">3</a>. For $m$ in the stated dyad, the following bound is uniform over the allowed $\lambda,\ell,\gamma$. There is a saving $c_G>0$ independent of the allowed $p_*$ and of $s_*$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, such that for all sufficiently large $N$, $$0\le F_*-f_m^0\le x^{4+c_G},\qquad F_*= f_{\rm spin}(t)+\tfrac14\int bq^2\,dv . \tag{G1}\label{eq:G1}$$* *Here $f_m^0=f_m(b,h_*)$, and $f_{\rm spin}(t)$ is the one-site scalar pressure with the same terminal mass $\ell$. The size threshold may depend on the fixed exponent choices.
  - Explanation: The unmasked, unseeded untilted trial gap improves strictly beyond the coarse fluctuation scale before local budgets are developed.
- **claim-residual-block-estimates** (bound, [source](#stmt-global-residual-blocks)): Fix a positive path law with terminal mass $a\in[1,4]$, and parametrize a deterministic increasing family of revealed cuts by $s$. At a cut $s$, let branches $\mathsf a,\mathsf b$ be conditionally independent continuations with their normalized positive kernels, given the common prefix. Partition their futures into the same $k$ deterministic blocks, the last ending at the terminal spin. Write $\Delta_j$ for the martingale increments, so that $y-X_s=\sum_{j=1}^k\Delta_j$, and let $\mu'_j\le a$ be the largest mass in block $j$. Evaluating $W_s$ on branch $\mathsf a$, we have $$W_s\le k\sum_{i,j}\mu'_j\, \mathbf E_{\mathsf b}[(\Delta_i^{\mathsf a}\cdot\Delta_j^{\mathsf b})^2\mid\mathsf a]. \label{eq:global-block-decomposition}$$ Conditioning on $\mathsf a$ retains its whole branch and the common prefix; only continuation $\mathsf b$ is averaged. For any deterministic interval $J$, any increment length $l>0$, and $q\ge1$, provided all indicated cuts exist, put $s_-=\inf J$ and $s_+=\sup J+2l$. Then $$\left\\|\int_J\|X_{s+2l}-X_{s+l}\|^2ds\right\\|_q \le C_q l\,\bigl\\|\|X_{s_+}-X_{s_-}\|^2\bigr\\|_q . \label{eq:global-grid}$$ The same estimate holds with increment $X_{s+l}-X_s$. For any nonnegative process $V_s$, not necessarily adapted, $$\left\\|\int\mathbf E_sV_s\,ds\right\\|_q \le C_q\left\\|\int V_s\,ds\right\\|_q . \label{eq:global-dual-doob}$$
  - Explanation: Deterministic blocking and martingale inequalities control residual Hessian observables and integrated increments under the full positive path law.
- **claim-buffer-brackets** (bound, [source](#stmt-global-buffer-brackets)): Fix a full single-path positive law with terminal mass $a\in[1,4]$ and deterministic revealed cuts. Let $w$ be one such cut, and let $\rho_-$, $\rho_+$ be deterministic probability measures supported on cuts before and after $w$, respectively. Write $$A_-=\int L_v\,\rho_-(dv),\qquad A_+=\int L_v\,\rho_+(dv).$$ Suppose that, for a deterministic number $\bar S$, $$\|S_v-\bar S\|\le\eta\quad \text{on the two buffers},\qquad \\|A_\pm-\mathbf EA_\pm\\|_p\le\varepsilon_p, \qquad 2\le p<\infty.$$ The bound on $S_v$ is required only almost everywhere for the two buffer measures. Then $$\bigl\\|\|X_w\|^2-\bar S\bigr\\|_p+ \left\\|\int\|X_w-X_v\|^2\rho_-(dv)\right\\|_p \le C(\eta+\varepsilon_p).$$ If two cuts $w,w'$ use the same earlier measure $\rho_-$, supported before both, and each has a later buffer satisfying the same hypotheses with the same $\bar S,\eta,\varepsilon_p$, then $$\bigl\\|\|X_w-X_{w'}\|^2\bigr\\|_p\le C(\eta+\varepsilon_p).$$
  - Explanation: Deterministic earlier and later buffers bound posterior norm fluctuations and increments; a common earlier buffer compares different cuts.
- **claim-weighted-comparison-budgets** (bound, [source](#stmt-bud-targets)): The averaging bounds needed are, on all segments of Proposition <a href="#prop:increment" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:increment">15</a>, uniformly, $$\mathbf E_\gamma\left[\max_{U\lesssim u\lesssim1} u\int_{v\asymp u} A_v\,dv\right]\lesssim_\circ U^4, \tag{C1}\label{eq:C1}$$ where one can use ordinary dyads with fixed comparable enlargements, and on size paths in addition $$\int (v^2+U^2)\mathbf E_\gamma A_v\,dv \le x^{4+c},\qquad f_{\rm spin}(K)+\int (K-h)^2/(4b)- f_m^0 \le x^{4+c}. \tag{C2}\label{eq:C2}$$ The second assertion of <a href="#eq:C2" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:C2">[eq:C2]</a> is pointwise, with some $c>0$ independent of sufficiently small $p_*$.
  - Explanation: Parameter averaging supplies dyadic overlap budgets and a sharper final-strength trial-gap estimate on size paths.
- **claim-modified-optimizer-geometry** (classification, [source](#stmt-bud-geometry)): For every minimizer in <a href="#eq:C5" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:C5">[eq:C5]</a>, the first-variation potential can be normalized so that its derivative is $${\cal H}'=C(r)\big[(2-p)r-2(1-p)S-p B/r\big],\qquad p=-r C'/C . \tag{C6}\label{eq:C6}$$ The minimizing density equals the cap $M_j$ where $\mathcal H<0$ and the floor $\bar k$ where $\mathcal H>0$; the remaining points are contacts. Each cap has radius width at most $M_j^{-1}$. Outside the floor, apart from a null set of contact exceptions, $\|S-r\|\lesssim_\circ D+O(x^{90})$. At contacts where $C$ is constant, $S=r$; on every cap contained in that constant region, $\|S-r\|\le M_j^{-1}$. These conclusions are the parts of the geometry of (OpenAI 2026, Lemma 3.3, equations (9)–(10)) [[PE](#ref-PE)] that will be used below.
  - Explanation: The first-variation potential separates cap, floor, and contact regions and bounds mismatch outside the floor.
- **claim-coarse-optimizer-profile** (bound, [source](#stmt-bud-coarse-profile)): For every optimizer in <a href="#eq:C5" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:C5">[eq:C5]</a>, uniformly, $$r(v)\asymp v\ (w_c\le v\le1),\qquad \sup_{c u\le v\le C u}\|r(v)-q(v)\|=o(u) \tag{C7}\label{eq:C7}$$ for each fixed $0<c<C$ (fixed numeric multiples, not the removal profile).
  - Explanation: Every modified optimizer is comparable to mass above the cutoff and approaches the reference quantile on the tested bands.
- **claim-outer-regularity-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-bud-outer-moments)): For every fixed $2\le p<\infty$, at every specified revelation cut and fork, $$\\|X_v\\|_p\lesssim_p\sqrt{v+w},\qquad \\|Q_v\\|_p\lesssim_p v+w \tag{C8}\label{eq:C8}$$ where $Q_v$ is the overlap of a pair splitting at mass $v$. On a regular small radius band $J\asymp v$, $$\left\\|\int_J W_{\alpha(r)}\,dr\right\\|_{p/2} \lesssim_{p,\circ}x^6/C(v).$$ When a preceding regular projection interval of comparable scale fits, the synchronized two-branch residual has norm $O_{p,\circ}(x^3/(v\sqrt{C(v)}))$. The constants are uniform over optimizers with the stated outer bounds.
  - Explanation: Conditional on outer regularity, posterior and overlap moments, integrated residuals, and synchronized projections have uniform bounds.
- **claim-enhanced-floor-second-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-bud-outer-second)): Under the same outer-regularity hypotheses, on regular mass dyads, with $B_f=X^{3/2}\lambda^{s_0/2}\Lambda^{-5/12}$, $$(\operatorname{avg}D^2)^{1/2} \lesssim_\circ (x^6/(C(v)v))^{1/3}+x^3/(v\sqrt{C(v)}) +m^{\delta/2}v_*+{\bf1}_{v\asymp u}\,u B_f . \tag{C10}\label{eq:C10}$$ The average is normalized by the length of the mass dyad. The indicator denotes a fixed band covering the enhanced floor, when present. The constants are uniform over optimizers with the stated outer bounds.
  - Explanation: Dyadic second moments include separate contributions from ordinary geometry and the enhanced density floor.
- **claim-common-calibration-cut** (construction, [source](#stmt-bud-common-star)): On compact target bands with $cw\le v\le Cw$ and $r=O(w)$, $$\int D^2\,dv=o(w^3),\qquad \int D^2\,dr=o(w^3), \qquad \int_0^{C'W}D_v\,dv=o(w^2)$$ for every fixed $C'$. There is a deterministic nonfloor cut $*$ in a regular band of scale $W$, above any prescribed fixed multiple of $w$, for which $S_*\asymp W$ and $$D_*\le x^{c_*}w^2/W,\qquad \\|Q_*-S_*\\|_p\le C_p x^{c_*}W$$ for every fixed $p$ and some $c_*>0$ independent of $p$. The cut is chosen from deterministic second moments and geometry before spin sampling; it is the same cut for all these moment estimates.
  - Explanation: Deterministic moment estimates select a common nonfloor calibration cut before spin sampling, valid for all fixed moment orders.
- **claim-modified-constraint-closure** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-bud-modified-closure)): Along any fixed sequence of optimizers with the strong-removal hypotheses above and fixed outer-comparability constants, the following estimate holds for targets $i$ with $cw\le v_i\le Cw$ and $r_i\le Cw$, $$\label{eq:bud-coarse-closure} \frac{\|S_i-\Gamma_{\widehat K}(\widehat K_i)\|}{w^3} \le C'\{\varepsilon_m+(D_i/w)^\vartheta\}, \qquad \varepsilon_m\longrightarrow0,\quad\vartheta>0.$$ The constants and modulus are common to the fixed target band. Thus this difference is $O(w^3)$ throughout the band, and is $o(w^3)$ along any moving target with $D_i=o(w)$. Since the target-band integrals of $D^2$ are $o(w^3)$, the same modulus gives, separately in the two coordinates, $$\label{eq:bud-coarse-closure-integrals} \frac1w\int \frac{\|S_i-\Gamma_{\widehat K}(\widehat K_i)\|}{w^3}\,dv_i=o(1), \qquad \frac1w\int \frac{\|S_{\alpha(r)}-\Gamma_{\widehat K}(\widehat K_{\alpha(r)})\|} {w^3}\,dr=o(1).$$ Each integral is restricted to the target band just described.
  - Explanation: Under strong removal and outer comparability, target discrepancies satisfy a common modulus and vanish after separate mass and radius averaging.
- **claim-finite-profile-strengthening** (bound, [source](#stmt-bud-strengthening)): On a slightly smaller interval interior to $I_j$, at each stage, $$\|\alpha-\beta_0\|\lesssim u a_j Z \tag{C12}\label{eq:C12}$$ for almost every global parameter, simultaneously for all its optimizers, where $Z\ge1$ has bounded averaged square in that parameter. For each fixed choice of the other path data, the exceptional set is independent of the optimizer and may be taken common to the finitely many stages. At successive stages that parameter may be restricted to slightly smaller fixed interior intervals, always leaving room beyond $[1/3,2/3]$; parameters not explicitly varied need no restriction beyond those of <a href="#eq:C3" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:C3">[eq:C3]</a>. At stage $-1$ the analogous assertion holds by <a href="#eq:C7" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:C7">[eq:C7]</a> with $Z=1$.
  - Explanation: A finite induction improves every optimizer outside a common exceptional parameter set using an averaged-square majorant.
- **claim-common-minimizer-envelope** (bound, [source](#stmt-bud-envelope)): Suppose the preceding stage satisfies <a href="#eq:C12" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:C12">[eq:C12]</a>. At the new stage the average optimized excess is at most $O(x^{4-2\zeta}u\Lambda^{1/3})$. For almost every global parameter, every minimizer simultaneously satisfies <a href="#eq:C13" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:C13">[eq:C13]</a> below, with a common measurable majorant $Z$ whose averaged square is bounded.
  - Explanation: Preceding accuracy pays for the next floor and produces one measurable derivative majorant for all current minimizers.
- **claim-buffer-scalar-curvature** (bound, [source](#stmt-bud-curvature)): By the scalar second derivative identity we now have uniformly a.e. in the inner buffer $$\frac{d^2}{dr^2}\big[\Gamma_s(k_*(r))-r\big] =-A_* (\widetilde\alpha(r)-\beta_0(r))+o(d_0), \tag{C14}\label{eq:C14}$$ where $A_*$ converges to a positive constant ($2(V_{*,zz}(0,0))^3 k_*'(0)^2$).
  - Explanation: Within the buffered violation, scalar curvature tracks the discrepancy of the modified and reference inverse profiles.
- **claim-moving-box-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-bud-box-moments)): Uniformly inside the buffer and for these averages, for every fixed moment order, we have $$\\|\delta_i\\|_p\lesssim_p d_0,\qquad \operatorname{avg}\\|\delta_i\\|_2^2\lesssim d_0^2\lambda^{0.14},\qquad \operatorname{avg}\\|Q_i-\|X_i\|^2\\|_2^2 \lesssim_\circ \lambda^{-\rho}u^2 A^3. \tag{C15}\label{eq:C15}$$
  - Explanation: Both specified box measures admit pointwise centered moments, averaged variance savings, and alias control.
- **claim-integrated-free-fork-errors** (bound, [source](#stmt-bud-free-forks)): Uniformly, $$\begin{split} \int_0^{c_Hu}D_v dv&\lesssim_\circ u^2 T_1,\qquad T_1=A+B_f+y_c^2,\\ \int_0^{c_Hu}D_v^2dv&\lesssim_\circ u^3 T_2,\quad T_2=A^2+B_f^2+A^{3/2}y_c+A y_c^{5/3},\\ (\operatorname{avg}_{v\sim w}D_v^2)^{1/2}&\lesssim_\circ u A \quad (w\ge c_Hu). \end{split} \tag{C16}\label{eq:C16}$$
  - Explanation: Free-fork errors have integrated and dyadic bounds retaining the contribution of broad caps.
- **claim-high-projection-primitives** (bound, [source](#stmt-bud-high-primitive)): Work in the buffered violation constructed above, with $d_0=uL$, $L\ge a_{\rm goal}Z$, $h_1=u\max(L,\sqrt\lambda)$, and $G_1=\min(\max(L^2,\lambda),\Lambda)$. Here $Z\ge1$ is the deterministic majorant in the global parameter from Lemma <a href="#bud:envelope" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="bud:envelope">34</a>; it is not a random variable under the positive spin law. For a high dyad $v\sim w\ge c_Hu$, replace an overlap at the observed buffer fork by the inner product of the two branches projected to a fixed cut of order $w$, after their separation and strictly before the dyad. In each fixed moment the cost is at most $$O_{p,\circ}(z_w),\qquad z_w=x^3\min\{(w\sqrt{C(w)})^{-1},\lambda^{-1/2}w^{-2}\}. \tag{C17}\label{eq:C17}$$ The integral of $L_v-\mathbb EL_v$ over a high dyad, against any deterministic weight bounded by one, has $L^2$ norm $o(u^2G_1)$, with a fixed power saving. This includes the plateau for every edge multiplier used on the comparison path.
  - Explanation: High-fork projections and centered primitives gain a strict power relative to the buffered target, including plateau contributions.
- **claim-strict-power-margins** (bound, [source](#stmt-bud-power-margins)): For clarity, here is some power accounting used here and below (write $\ll$ in such estimates for polynomial gains). Uniformly under <a href="#eq:C4" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:C4">[eq:C4]</a>, <a href="#eq:C11" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:C11">[eq:C11]</a>, $a_{\rm goal}Z\le L\le1$, we have $$\begin{gathered} T_2,\ A T_1,\ X^3 A\Lambda^{-1/3}\lambda^{-1/6}, \ \lambda^{-2\rho}A^3\ \ll P_1,\qquad \lambda^{0.06}T_1,\ L T_1,\ X^3\Lambda^{-1/3}\lambda_1^{-1/6}Z^{1/6} \ \ll G_1 . \tag{C18}\label{eq:C18} \end{gathered}$$
  - Explanation: The specified exponent hierarchy leaves strict power margins for all displayed composite errors.
- **claim-buffered-row-closure** (bound, [source](#stmt-bud-closure)): In any of the boxes of <a href="#eq:C15" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:C15">[eq:C15]</a> we claim $$\operatorname{avg}\|S_i-\Gamma_s(K_s(i))\|=o(u^3 P_1). \tag{C19}\label{eq:C19}$$
  - Explanation: The buffered mean overlap matches its scalar response to an error small relative to the removal-strength budget.
- **claim-genuine-pointwise-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-statistics-pointwise)): Assume the direct-path hypotheses above and $Y=o(1)$, or their low-region size-path variant. For every fixed $1\le p<\infty$ the following estimates hold: $$\begin{array}{ll} \\|\|X_v\|^2\\|_p+\\|L_v\\|_p+\\|Q_{\rm split\ at\ }v\\|_p\lesssim_p v+Y;\\ \\|Q_{\rm split\ at\ }v-q(v)\\|_p+ \\|2L_v-q(v)\\|_p+\\|\|X_v\|^2-q(v)\\|_p\lesssim_{p,\diamond} e(v) & (v\gtrsim Y). \end{array} \tag{D2}\label{eq:D2}$$ In the low-region variant the second line is only low. $e$ is deterministic conditional on the parameters, with, on each such dyad $v\asymp r$, $$x^C\le e(v)\lesssim r,\qquad \int e(v)^2\,dv/r\lesssim_\diamond m_r^2,\qquad m_r=Y^2/r.$$ On those regions $\|d(v)\|+\|\dot d(v)\|\lesssim_\diamond\lambda r^2 e(v)$, by the corresponding path estimates. At $v\lesssim Y$ use $r=e=Y$ in this last assertion and <a href="#eq:D2" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:D2">[eq:D2]</a>.
  - Explanation: Genuine-path overlaps and posterior observables obey raw moments and deterministic-envelope errors in the stated direct or low-region regime.
- **claim-deterministic-width-construction** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-statistics-widths)): The preceding construction gives a deterministic envelope with the size, integral, and defect bounds stated in Proposition <a href="#prop:statistics-pointwise" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:statistics-pointwise">41</a>. The random moment bounds <a href="#eq:D2" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:D2">[eq:D2]</a> will be proved in the next subsection. The widths and windows have the following additional properties.* 1. *At comparable points, $\mathfrak h(z')\lesssim\mathfrak h(z)+\|z'-z\|$, with comparability of widths when $\|z'-z\|$ is a sufficiently small fraction of $\mathfrak h(z)$. Also $x^C\le\mathfrak h\lesssim r$, $e\gtrsim b_\epsilon Y^2/r$, $\|f\|\lesssim b_\epsilon^{-1}e$, and $\int_{\rm band}G_z(\mathfrak h/r)^2 dz/r\lesssim_\diamond(U/r)^4$.* 2. *Unless $Z^2\mathfrak h\gtrsim b_\epsilon r$, there are past and future windows of $z$-length comparable to $\mathfrak h$, adjacent or at that distance, each with average $G_*$ there satisfying $$\sup G_z\lesssim G_*,\qquad G_*(\mathfrak h/r)^3\gtrsim (U/r)^6 . \tag{D4}\label{eq:D4}$$ They can be taken small fixed fractions of the indicated scales. From such a nontrivial point there is also remaining forward $z$-length at least a small fixed macroscopic constant (for taking longer layers up to a macroscopic mass), with <a href="#eq:D3" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:D3">[eq:D3]</a> holding using each successive scale.* 3. *Partition any full band as above into consecutive tiles of lengths comparable to $\mathfrak h$, with this width and $e$ comparable over each tile. Writing $\mu_I=\int_I G_z dz/r$, $$\sup_I G_z\lesssim b_\epsilon^{-C}(r\mu_I/\|I\|+x^K),\quad \Delta_I S\lesssim b_\epsilon^{-1}\min(r,Z^2 \|I\|),\quad \sum_I \sup_I(e/r)^2\lesssim Z^2 . \tag{D5}\label{eq:D5}$$ The variation assertion holds also on comparable-scale enlargements of these tiles within the path.
  - Explanation: Deterministic widths yield compatible buffers, tile variation bounds, and an integrated envelope budget before random moment estimates are applied.
- **claim-integrated-overlap-variances** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-statistics-integrated)): For every fixed integer $k\ge0$, the following bounds hold. All quantities on the right are untilted; in particular this convention applies to $S,D$: $$\begin{split} \mathbf E\int W\,e(v)^{2k}\,dv/r &\lesssim_\diamond (z_r^0)^2 Z_h^2 r^3 \begin{cases}1& k=0,\\ m_r^2 r^{2k-2}& k\ge1,\end{cases}\\ \int \mathbf E[X^{\mathsf T} C_v X+\operatorname{tr}C_v^2]\,dv/r &\lesssim_\diamond (z_r^0)^2 Z_h^2 r^2,\qquad \int D_v^2\,dv/r\lesssim_\diamond z_r^0 Z_h r^2 . \end{split} \tag{D7}\label{eq:D7}$$
  - Explanation: Untilting conventions and deterministic tiles control weighted residual integrals, conditional covariance terms, and overlap variances.
- **claim-large-envelope-localization** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-statistics-localized)): There is also a localized bound for the direct path. For any sufficiently small fixed $\delta'>0$, on all the bands in <a href="#eq:D7" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:D7">[eq:D7]</a> together, $$\int_{\{e(v)\ge x^{\delta'}\}} D_v^2\,dv \lesssim_\diamond x^{-C_0\delta'} z_1^0 Y^2 Z^2 \tag{D8}\label{eq:D8}$$ with an absolute finite loss exponent $C_0$ independent of $\delta'$.
  - Explanation: Direct-path variance can be localized to large-envelope regions with a loss exponent independent of the chosen small threshold exponent.
- **claim-lower-band-variances** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-statistics-lower-band)): At $v\le C Y$ we will discard $v<x$ or treat it by raw bounds. For dyads of size $w\lesssim Y$ restricted to $v\ge x$, put $\epsilon_w=x^3\sqrt Y/(\sqrt{\lambda_1}\max(w,U)^{3/2})$, $E_0=g_B Y^2=x^3\sqrt Y/(\sqrt{\lambda_1}U^{3/2})$. Then $$\int_{v\asymp w,\ v\ge x}\mathbf EW\,dv\lesssim\epsilon_w^2,\qquad \int_{v\asymp w,\ v\ge x} D_v^2\,dv\lesssim_\circ Y\epsilon_w. \tag{D9}\label{eq:D9}$$
  - Explanation: Source inequalities and mass slides control lower-band residual and variance integrals above the mask.
- **claim-centered-polynomial-integrals** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-statistics-centered)): Fix a dyad $v\asymp r$, $r\gtrsim Y$, and a deterministic polynomial $P_v$ of total degree $j\ge1$ in the centered inserted value. Assume its remaining deterministic powers are bounded by the corresponding powers of $e(v)$. Then the centered integral using $2L_v$ on one path satisfies $$\left\\|\frac1r\int [P_v(2L_v-S_v)-\mathbf EP_v(2L_v-S_v)]\,dv\right\\|_2 \lesssim_\diamond z_r^0 r Z_h \begin{cases}1& j=1,\\ m_r r^{j-2}& j\ge2.\end{cases} \tag{D10}\label{eq:D10}$$ Here the coefficient of degree $i$ can be any deterministic function bounded by $C e(v)^{j-i}$.
  - Explanation: Deterministic polynomial coefficients and envelope powers yield centered integral bounds under a full single-path law.
- **claim-common-low-projection** (bound, [source](#stmt-cor-statistics-low-projection)): One more consequence of <a href="#eq:A3" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A3">[eq:A3]</a>, <a href="#eq:D2" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:D2">[eq:D2]</a> is the following: for $Y\lesssim c'$ up to a sufficiently small fixed scale, a pair split well before $c'$ (say mass $\le c'/8$) changes in overlap by at most $O_{p,\circ}(z_{c'}^0 c')$ in every fixed moment upon projecting down from later cuts to mass $c'$.
  - Explanation: A pair separating sufficiently before the common low cut can be projected there with a controlled fixed-moment error.
- **claim-coarse-and-multiplier-contributions** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-statistics-coarse-switch)): For sufficiently small fixed $\kappa>0$, the direct-strength contribution from $Y>x^\kappa$ satisfies the direct part of Proposition <a href="#prop:increment" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:increment">15</a>. The two final-strength multiplier changes also satisfy its required power-saving bound.
  - Explanation: Large derived scales and final multiplier changes are controlled separately from the refined small-scale pressure expansion.
- **claim-size-path-all-moment-accuracy** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-statistics-size-accuracy)): Here $\lambda=x^{p_*}$; assume $p_*$ sufficiently small. Uniformly at every parameter value on smoothed size paths in the untilted system there is a fixed $\delta_*>0$, available independently of further decreases in $p_*$, such that $$\sup_v\\|Q-q(v)\\|_p\le C_p x^{\delta_*} \tag{D11}\label{eq:D11}$$ for a pair split at $v$, for **every** fixed $p$.
  - Explanation: Smoothed size paths have uniform overlap accuracy with a saving fixed before subsequent decreases of the strength exponent.
- **claim-low-scale-deterministic-cap** (bound, [source](#stmt-cor-statistics-cap)): For <a href="#eq:D1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:D1">[eq:D1]</a> and the low statistics on size paths we may cap $Y$ at $x^{\delta_*/3}$, decreasing $p_*$ if necessary, and still write $Y=UZ$. Indeed <a href="#eq:D11" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:D11">[eq:D11]</a> gives $\|S_v-q(v)\|^2\lesssim x^{2\delta_*}$, whereas on every bounded band $$x^{2\delta_*}\lesssim x^{4\delta_*/3}/r^2.$$ Thus the capped scale still satisfies <a href="#eq:D1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:D1">[eq:D1]</a>. Its new majorant $Z=\min(Z_{\rm old},x^{\delta_*/3}/U)$ is at least one and no larger than the old majorant, so its fourth parameter moment is preserved.
  - Explanation: The low scale can be capped deterministically while preserving the mean-error budget and its parameter moment.
- **claim-high-mass-means-variances** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-statistics-high)): Take $Z$ as at the end of <a href="#eq:D11" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:D11">[eq:D11]</a>; by <a href="#eq:C2" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:C2">[eq:C2]</a> take also $Z_g\ge1,\ \mathbf E_\gamma Z_g^2\lesssim1$ with $\int v^2\nu[(Q-q)^2]\,dv\le x^{4+c} Z_g^2$ untilted. Choose $$V_i=x^{a_i}\quad(0\le i\le2),\qquad p_*\ll a_2\ll a_1\ll a_0\ll\min(c,\delta_*).$$ There are fixed $b_H>0,C_H<\infty$, with $b_H\gg C_Ha_1,\ a_1\gg C_Ha_2$, for which $$\sup_{v\ge V_1}\|f(v)\|\le x^{2+b_H}(Z^2+Z_g),\qquad D_{H,i}:=\sup_{v\ge V_i}D_v\le x^{3-C_H a_i}Z^2\quad(i=1,2). \tag{D15}\label{eq:D15}$$
  - Explanation: Final-strength high-mass means and variances gain sharper powers through centered low-source control and pair inversion.
- **claim-low-sources-retained-pair** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-statistics-low-sources)): Consider an allocation with bounded degree and bounded topology weights. The old prescribed topology is either absent or consists of one pair splitting at mass at least $V_i$; in particular it contains no prescribed low fork. Call designated factors at $v<V_i$ low. Each low factor is either stochastic, of the form $\delta=Q-S_v$, or deterministic, bounded by $O_\diamond(e(v))$, with $e=Y$ for $v\lesssim Y$. There is at least one stochastic low factor and no stochastic factor at a higher mass. Deterministic factors at higher masses may be included in the coefficient. If there is exactly one low factor, assume that its coefficient is $O_\diamond(v)$. Projected pairs whose endpoints are already on separate branches are allowed, with the convention following <a href="#eq:D9" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:D9">[eq:D9]</a>.* *There are two conclusions. In the untilted law, test the product by $P=Q_{ab}-S_{ab}$ for the prescribed high pair. Alternatively, compare its tilted and untilted expectations on the stop, with no $P$, using $\delta^*=Q^*-S_v$ in the tilted law and the same deterministic coefficients in both laws. After signed integration the respective bounds are $$O_\diamond(x^3\lambda^{-C}Z^2){\cal P}+O(x^K), \qquad {\cal P}=D_{ab}\ \hbox{or respectively }1. \tag{D16}\label{eq:D16}$$ The negligible error exponent $K$ can be arbitrarily large.* *Extra auxiliary slots are permitted. On each fixed tree shape the absolute joint density of freely placed distinct fork vertices is bounded; deterministic weights and restrictions may depend on all their times. An additional multiplier depending only on the high times can be factored out and integrated separately. Ties to a low vertex reuse its freely integrated coordinate, by the signed rule; no initially free low fork requires an atomic time measure. This distinction concerns the underlying allocation measure. The old high fork may carry its prescribed atom. A new low fork is instead a free coordinate with bounded density; later attachments to it reuse that coordinate. Merely having the same mass as a different vertex supplies no additional atom. The argument below retains this distinction before discarding deterministic restrictions in absolute estimates.
  - Explanation: Centered low sources retain the exact second norm of a prescribed high pair, or cancel between stopped ensembles, using a fixed marginal law.
- **claim-centered-allocation-saving** (bound, [source](#stmt-exp-lem-centered-count)): Fix $j\ge2$ pair factors. Each factor is either $\delta$, possibly projected, or a deterministic function bounded by $O_\diamond(e(v))$; use $e=Y$ on the lower band. Fix the bands, their order, and every projection cut. Each projection cut lies after the split of its pair. Let $s=1,\ldots,l$ index the distinct vertices to which these factors are assigned, with multiplicities $k_s$ and band scales $r_s$, and put $w=\max_s r_s$. Suppose that the deterministic weights are common to both ensembles and, on each of boundedly many topology shapes, are bounded by $$O_\diamond(\lambda w^{5-j})\ \prod_{s=1}^l dv_s/w, \tag{E2}\label{eq:E1}$$ times measures of bounded volume in the other integration variables. These are product majorants, so deterministic restrictions may be retained. If $j=l=2$, assume in addition the factor $O_\diamond(\min_s r_s/w)$. More explicitly, if $H$ is this deterministic weight and $T_i^{\mathrm{tilt}},T_i^0$ are the pair factors in the two ensembles, we estimate $$\int H\left\{\nu^{\mathrm{tilt}} \left[\prod_{i=1}^jT_i^{\mathrm{tilt}}\right] -\nu^0\left[\prod_{i=1}^jT_i^0\right]\right\}.$$ The weight, deterministic factors, cuts, and centering $S$ are common; only the positive law and the masked overlap vary. The absolute value of this difference is bounded by $$O_\diamond\big(\lambda Y^5(x/Y+g_B)\big)+O(x^K) \tag{E3}\label{eq:E2}$$ where $K$ can be arbitrarily large. Indeed the two contributions are $$\lambda Y^5\frac{x}{Y}=x^5\lambda^{1-2s_*}Z^4, \qquad \lambda Y^5g_B=x^5\lambda^{(1-\eta)/2-s_*}Z^{7/2}.$$ Both powers of $\lambda$ are positive. Since $\mathbf E_\gamma Z^4\lesssim_\circ1$, the averaged bound is $O(x^{5+c'})$ for some $c'>0$, after taking the allowed losses smaller than these gains.
  - Explanation: Deterministic allocation majorants and centered moment gains yield an averaged pressure saving for all allowed multiplicity patterns.
- **claim-compressed-low-degree-coefficients** (bound, [source](#stmt-exp-prop-low-coefficients)): Fix the dyadic restrictions on the base factors and a cut $c\gg w$ within the region where the small inverse is regular. A sufficiently large fixed separation factor is enough; on size paths require also $c\lesssim\lambda$. Group base slots into blocks that share their path through $c$. Their split tree below $c$ is the *skeleton*, and every designated pair joins distinct blocks.* *Apply the operator ${\cal O}$ defined above to the pressure polynomial <a href="#eq:E3" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:E3">[eq:E3]</a>: it is $1+\partial_\theta$, with the formal action $\partial_\theta\Delta=-\Delta/6$, on a size path, and $\partial_{\log\lambda}$, holding $\Delta$ fixed, on a direct path. Group the resulting signed allocation coefficients by this skeleton and sum their internal placements within each block. The bound below concerns these differentiated, grouped coefficients. This is a rearrangement of a signed measure. The probabilistic expectations used to evaluate the coefficients remain positive scalar laws on each fixed topology. The spin-model pair tests have been projected to $c$, or to a neighboring smaller cut, so they depend only on the skeleton and can be kept outside the internal sums. For $j=2,3,4$, the resulting coefficient, including the skeleton allocation weight, is bounded by $$O_\diamond(\lambda c^{5-j})\prod_{s\ {\rm skeleton\ fork}} dv_s/c . \tag{E4}\label{eq:E4}$$ If $j=2$, the designated vertices are distinct, and $c\asymp w$, the bound includes the further factor $O_\diamond(\min_s r_s/c)$. A factor $d$ or $\dot d$ may first contribute $\lambda c^2$ to the coefficient, leaving a deterministic factor bounded by the ordinary envelope because $r\lesssim c$. Like $b$ and $\dot b$, these weights are constant during each internal block sum.* *Combine contributions only when they multiply the same product of pair tests on the same skeleton. In particular, this combines a repeated pair with the square counterterm. Give such terms the same dyadic restrictions and projection cuts. The cut, shape, and mass coordinates are fixed during coefficient differentiation. Internal summation may then be done before or after that differentiation. The spin tests receive only the formal action on $\Delta$ already specified: project the differentiated polynomial, without differentiating a random test or a projection law.
  - Explanation: Internal signed scalar sums and the formal path operator cancel the leading low-degree coefficients before absolute bounds are taken.

Write $\\langle\\cdot\\rangle_{g,h}$ for expectation under the product of that model’s Gibbs laws with disorders $g,h$, and $R=n^{-1}\\sum_i\\sigma_i\\tau_i$ for the overlap. Thus the replicas are independent conditional on their disorders; $\\mathbb E$ below also averages the disorder and any replacement set.*\n\n\n\n*For $t>0$, set $g^t=e^{-t}g+\\sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}\\,g'$. The following bounds hold uniformly for sufficiently large $N$. Every derivative order and compact time interval is fixed before $N\\to\\infty$.*\n\n*For the direct reference, the normalized inverse near zero has uniformly bounded one-sided derivatives of every fixed order. Their $\\log\\lambda$ derivatives are $O(\\lambda)$, and $$\\partial_{\\log\\lambda}q(v)=O(\\lambda\\min(v,1)).$$ At fixed sufficiently small normalized time $\\xi$, the $\\log\\lambda$ derivative of $1-\\widehat\\Gamma'(\\xi)/\\widehat\\Gamma'(0)$ is $O(\\lambda\\xi^2)$.*\n\n\n*For the smoothed reference, write $\\widehat V_j$ and $\\widehat\\Gamma_j$ to display the terminal mass $j=4/\\ell$. The physical initial spatial derivatives obey the rescaling bound, for each fixed $r\\ge1$, $$\\left|\\partial_\\theta\\left(\n     \\ell^{1-r}\\partial_z^r V(0,0)\\right)\\right|\n \\le C_r e^{-c_rM}.$$*\n\n*Over the full mass interval $(0,4)$, the smoothed clocks $t,q$ are absolutely continuous in $\\theta$, with $$\\int_0^4\\bigl(|\\partial_\\theta t(v)|\n                  +|\\partial_\\theta q(v)|\\bigr)\\,dv\n \\le C M^C.                                            \\tag{P2b}\\label{eq:P2b}$$ The constants in this integrated bound contain no inverse power of $\\omega$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-red-prop-moments",
        "exact_quote": "Assume Proposition <a href=\"#prop:increment\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:increment\">15</a>. For every fixed integer $k\\ge1$, the moments $\\mathbb EY_n^k$ converge at a positive power rate. Their limiting second moment is finite and strictly positive, and the centered variables $Y_n$ have uniformly bounded exponential moments on some constant neighborhood of the origin. They converge weakly to a moment-determinate law. Removing the completion and standardizing by the exact finite-size variance gives the convergence asserted in Theorem <a href=\"#thm:main\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:main\">1</a>.",

        "exact_quote": "The kernel <a href=\"#eq:A8\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:A8\">[eq:A8]</a> is considered on extensions of any *fixed* finite list of old labels. A pair function $u_{ab}$ may depend on the topology with those labels but ignores any unused extra labels (is pulled back by restriction). Indices in this section used as pair arguments are distinct leaves. Normalize terminal mass to 1; other bounded terminal masses reduce to this by mass rescaling, scaling cumulative covariances by the square of the mass. Take a monotone step scalar path $K$, nonnegative bounded-variation step multiplier $b$, and retain pair levels in a terminal interval of the hierarchy (the whole interval is allowed). Suppose at these levels $$1-b_r\\mathbf E\\chi_r^2\\ge e>0,\\qquad \\chi_r=V_{zz}(K_r,Z_{K_r}).$$ Bounds called polynomial in this section are in $1+K_{\\rm top}+\\|b\\|_\\infty+\\operatorname{var}b+e^{-1}$, independent of the number of steps. On the retained levels $$u_{ab}\\ \\longmapsto\\ u_{ab}-\\sum_{cd\\ {\\rm retained}}{\\bf M}_{ab,cd} b_{cd}u_{cd}\n                                                                     \\tag{H1}\\label{eq:H1}$$ has an inverse on each finite step resolution. Each output is an integral of inputs over allocations of up to two more labels (some arguments can also be reused), with weights dominated by a polynomial times the ordinary *absolute* unrestricted attachment rules to the old tree including $ab$. Restrictions and bounded weights can depend on the topology. This formulation in particular controls new split densities, allowing coincidences and ties to existing forks. It applies with $ab$ using old labels too. We only need symmetric arrays (on antisymmetric ones the subtracted sum is zero).",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-inv-sector-response",
        "exact_quote": "Use the finite resolution above, and put $m_t=V_z(K_t,Z_{K_t})$, $\\chi_t=V_{zz}(K_t,Z_{K_t})$. Let $\\mathbf E_t$ condition on the scalar prefix through $K_t$. On the row-zero sector, different sheets do not mix. On sheet $r$, the multiplier in the child resolutions $\\widetilde E_i^r\\otimes\\widetilde E_l^r$, $i,l\\ge r+1$, is $$g_r^{il}=\\mathbf E[(\\mathbf E_r\\chi_{i-1})\n                         (\\mathbf E_r\\chi_{l-1})].$$ On the additive sector associated with $E_k$, the action on sheet coefficients is $$({\\bf M}^k f)_r=g_r^k f_r-\\sum_t B^k_{rt}\\mu_t^k f_t,\\qquad\n g_t^k=\\mathbf E[\\chi_t\\chi_{\\max(k-1,t)}].\n \\tag{H2}\\label{eq:H2}$$ Here $A=K_{k-1}$, with $A=0$ for $k=0$, and $$B^k_{rt}=\\mathbf E\\left[\n   \\operatorname{Hess}_{z,\\alpha}V(A,Z_A)[\\beta_r,\\beta_t]\\right],\n \\qquad\n \\beta_t=\\begin{cases}\n (m_t,0),&t<k,\\\\\n (0,\\delta_{K_t}),&t\\ge k.\n \\end{cases}$$ The Hessian varies the starting field and the subsequent mass profile. The prefix values $m_t$, $t<k$, are held fixed during this differentiation, and $\\delta_{K_t}$ denotes an impulse in the subsequent profile. Expectation is taken after evaluating the Hessian. The matrix $B^k$ is positive semidefinite. Restricting either action to retained levels discards the other input and output sheets.*\n\n*The kernels $B^k,g^k$ are bounded and Lipschitz in their evaluation times with polynomial constants. Their changes with the resolution index satisfy $$\\|B^{k+1}-B^k\\|_\\infty+\\|g^{k+1}-g^k\\|_\\infty\n \\lesssim_{\\rm pol}p_k(K_k-K_{k-1}).$$ A successive difference of $g_r^{il}$ in index $i$ is bounded by $Cp_i(K_i-K_{i-1})$; a mixed difference is bounded by the product of the corresponding two bounds. Moreover $0\\le g_r^k,g_r^{il}\\le\\mathbf E\\chi_r^2$. These formulas apply with arbitrary old-label topologies under the coefficient convention just described. For $k=0$, their Hessian kernel also satisfies $$|B^0_{rt}|\\lesssim C(1+K_{R+1})^C K_{\\min(r,t)}$$ when the earlier evaluation time is small.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-global-residual-blocks",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a positive path law with terminal mass $a\\in[1,4]$, and parametrize a deterministic increasing family of revealed cuts by $s$. At a cut $s$, let branches $\\mathsf a,\\mathsf b$ be conditionally independent continuations with their normalized positive kernels, given the common prefix. Partition their futures into the same $k$ deterministic blocks, the last ending at the terminal spin. Write $\\Delta_j$ for the martingale increments, so that $y-X_s=\\sum_{j=1}^k\\Delta_j$, and let $\\mu'_j\\le a$ be the largest mass in block $j$. Evaluating $W_s$ on branch $\\mathsf a$, we have $$W_s\\le k\\sum_{i,j}\\mu'_j\\,\n    \\mathbf E_{\\mathsf b}[(\\Delta_i^{\\mathsf a}\\cdot\\Delta_j^{\\mathsf b})^2\\mid\\mathsf a].\n \\label{eq:global-block-decomposition}$$ Conditioning on $\\mathsf a$ retains its whole branch and the common prefix; only continuation $\\mathsf b$ is averaged. For any deterministic interval $J$, any increment length $l>0$, and $q\\ge1$, provided all indicated cuts exist, put $s_-=\\inf J$ and $s_+=\\sup J+2l$. Then $$\\left\\|\\int_J|X_{s+2l}-X_{s+l}|^2ds\\right\\|_q\n       \\le C_q l\\,\\bigl\\||X_{s_+}-X_{s_-}|^2\\bigr\\|_q .\n \\label{eq:global-grid}$$ The same estimate holds with increment $X_{s+l}-X_s$. For any nonnegative process $V_s$, not necessarily adapted, $$\\left\\|\\int\\mathbf E_sV_s\\,ds\\right\\|_q\n       \\le C_q\\left\\|\\int V_s\\,ds\\right\\|_q .\n \\label{eq:global-dual-doob}$$",
        "source_id": "PM-217.1"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-global-buffer-brackets",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a full single-path positive law with terminal mass $a\\in[1,4]$ and deterministic revealed cuts. Let $w$ be one such cut, and let $\\rho_-$, $\\rho_+$ be deterministic probability measures supported on cuts before and after $w$, respectively. Write $$A_-=\\int L_v\\,\\rho_-(dv),\\qquad\n A_+=\\int L_v\\,\\rho_+(dv).$$ Suppose that, for a deterministic number $\\bar S$, $$|S_v-\\bar S|\\le\\eta\\quad\n  \\text{on the two buffers},\\qquad\n \\|A_\\pm-\\mathbf EA_\\pm\\|_p\\le\\varepsilon_p,\n \\qquad 2\\le p<\\infty.$$ The bound on $S_v$ is required only almost everywhere for the two buffer measures. Then $$\\bigl\\||X_w|^2-\\bar S\\bigr\\|_p+\n \\left\\|\\int|X_w-X_v|^2\\rho_-(dv)\\right\\|_p\n       \\le C(\\eta+\\varepsilon_p).$$ If two cuts $w,w'$ use the same earlier measure $\\rho_-$, supported before both, and each has a later buffer satisfying the same hypotheses with the same $\\bar S,\\eta,\\varepsilon_p$, then $$\\bigl\\||X_w-X_{w'}|^2\\bigr\\|_p\\le C(\\eta+\\varepsilon_p).$$",
        "source_id": "PM-217.1"
      },

Then $$\\bigl\\||X_w|^2-\\bar S\\bigr\\|_p+\n \\left\\|\\int|X_w-X_v|^2\\rho_-(dv)\\right\\|_p\n       \\le C(\\eta+\\varepsilon_p).$$ If two cuts $w,w'$ use the same earlier measure $\\rho_-$, supported before both, and each has a later buffer satisfying the same hypotheses with the same $\\bar S,\\eta,\\varepsilon_p$, then $$\\bigl\\||X_w-X_{w'}|^2\\bigr\\|_p\\le C(\\eta+\\varepsilon_p).$$",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-bud-targets",
        "exact_quote": "The averaging bounds needed are, on all segments of Proposition <a href=\"#prop:increment\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:increment\">15</a>, uniformly, $$\\mathbf E_\\gamma\\left[\\max_{U\\lesssim u\\lesssim1}\n       u\\int_{v\\asymp u} A_v\\,dv\\right]\\lesssim_\\circ U^4,              \\tag{C1}\\label{eq:C1}$$ where one can use ordinary dyads with fixed comparable enlargements, and on size paths in addition $$\\int (v^2+U^2)\\mathbf E_\\gamma A_v\\,dv \\le x^{4+c},\\qquad\n f_{\\rm spin}(K)+\\int (K-h)^2/(4b)- f_m^0 \\le x^{4+c}.                  \\tag{C2}\\label{eq:C2}$$ The second assertion of <a href=\"#eq:C2\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:C2\">[eq:C2]</a> is pointwise, with some $c>0$ independent of sufficiently small $p_*$.",

      "conclusion": {

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-statistics-widths",
        "exact_quote": "The preceding construction gives a deterministic envelope with the size, integral, and defect bounds stated in Proposition <a href=\"#prop:statistics-pointwise\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:statistics-pointwise\">41</a>. The random moment bounds <a href=\"#eq:D2\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:D2\">[eq:D2]</a> will be proved in the next subsection. The widths and windows have the following additional properties.*\n\n1.  *At comparable points, $\\mathfrak h(z')\\lesssim\\mathfrak h(z)+|z'-z|$, with comparability of widths when $|z'-z|$ is a sufficiently small fraction of $\\mathfrak h(z)$. Also $x^C\\le\\mathfrak h\\lesssim r$, $e\\gtrsim b_\\epsilon Y^2/r$, $|f|\\lesssim b_\\epsilon^{-1}e$, and $\\int_{\\rm band}G_z(\\mathfrak h/r)^2 dz/r\\lesssim_\\diamond(U/r)^4$.*\n\n\n2.  *Unless $Z^2\\mathfrak h\\gtrsim b_\\epsilon r$, there are past and future windows of $z$-length comparable to $\\mathfrak h$, adjacent or at that distance, each with average $G_*$ there satisfying $$\\sup G_z\\lesssim G_*,\\qquad G_*(\\mathfrak h/r)^3\\gtrsim (U/r)^6 .          \\tag{D4}\\label{eq:D4}$$ They can be taken small fixed fractions of the indicated scales. From such a nontrivial point there is also remaining forward $z$-length at least a small fixed macroscopic constant (for taking longer layers up to a macroscopic mass), with <a href=\"#eq:D3\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:D3\">[eq:D3]</a> holding using each successive scale.*\n\n\n3.  *Partition any full band as above into consecutive tiles of lengths comparable to $\\mathfrak h$, with this width and $e$ comparable over each tile. Writing $\\mu_I=\\int_I G_z dz/r$, $$\\sup_I G_z\\lesssim b_\\epsilon^{-C}(r\\mu_I/|I|+x^K),\\quad\n     \\Delta_I S\\lesssim b_\\epsilon^{-1}\\min(r,Z^2 |I|),\\quad\n     \\sum_I \\sup_I(e/r)^2\\lesssim Z^2 .                                 \\tag{D5}\\label{eq:D5}$$ The variation assertion holds also on comparable-scale enlargements of these tiles within the path.",

        "exact_quote": "Consider an allocation with bounded degree and bounded topology weights. Each low factor is either stochastic, of the form $\\delta=Q-S_v$, or deterministic, bounded by $O_\\diamond(e(v))$, with $e=Y$ for $v\\lesssim Y$. There is at least one stochastic low factor and no stochastic factor at a higher mass. Deterministic factors at higher masses may be included in the coefficient. If there is exactly one low factor, assume that its coefficient is $O_\\diamond(v)$. Projected pairs whose endpoints are already on separate branches are allowed, with the convention following <a href=\"#eq:D9\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:D9\">[eq:D9]</a>.*\n\n\n*There are two conclusions. In the untilted law, test the product by $P=Q_{ab}-S_{ab}$ for the prescribed high pair. Alternatively, compare its tilted and untilted expectations on the stop, with no $P$, using $\\delta^*=Q^*-S_v$ in the tilted law and the same deterministic coefficients in both laws. After signed integration the respective bounds are $$O_\\diamond(x^3\\lambda^{-C}Z^2){\\cal P}+O(x^K),\n \\qquad {\\cal P}=D_{ab}\\ \\hbox{or respectively }1.                 \\tag{D16}\\label{eq:D16}$$ The negligible error exponent $K$ can be arbitrarily large.*\n\n*Extra auxiliary slots are permitted. On each fixed tree shape the absolute joint density of freely placed distinct fork vertices is bounded; deterministic weights and restrictions may depend on all their times. An additional multiplier depending only on the high times can be factored out and integrated separately. Ties to a low vertex reuse its freely integrated coordinate, by the signed rule; no initially free low fork requires an atomic time measure. This distinction concerns the underlying allocation measure. The old high fork may carry its prescribed atom. A new low fork is instead a free coordinate with bounded density; later attachments to it reuse that coordinate. Merely having the same mass as a different vertex supplies no additional atom. The argument below retains this distinction before discarding deterministic restrictions in absolute estimates.",

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Gaussian Ising SK model and standardized free energy** ([source](#eq:model)): Let $(g_{ij})_{1\le i<j\le n}$ be independent standard Gaussian variables. For $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n$ and $\beta>1$, put $$\label{eq:model} H_n(\sigma)=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i<j}g_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j, \qquad Z_n(\beta)=\sum_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n}e^{\beta H_n(\sigma)}, \qquad F_n(\beta)=\log Z_n(\beta).$$
- **Gaussian completion and scaled centered free energy** ([source](#eq:completed-free-energy)): Let $\zeta_n$ be a centered Gaussian of variance $\beta^2/2$, independent of the couplings, and define $$\label{eq:completed-free-energy} F_n^c=F_n(\beta)-n\log2+\zeta_n, \qquad Y_n=n^{-1/6}(F_n^c-\mathbb E F_n^c).$$
- **Positive tree law** ([source](#pm-h-10)): We call this the *positive tree law* and write $\nu[P]$ for its expectation of $P$, including both fields and terminal spins.
- **Subpower loss** ([source](#pm-h-10)): We use “with subpower loss” or $\lesssim_\circ$ to allow $C_\epsilon x^{-\epsilon}$ for *every* sufficiently small fixed $\epsilon>0$.
- **Power small** ([source](#pm-h-10)): “Power small” means $O(x^c)$ for some fixed $c>0$; for assertions in every fixed $L^p$ a power saving not indexed by $p$ means the exponent is independent of the fixed finite moment order (constant and threshold need not be).
- **Signed allocation per root mass** ([source](#pm-h-12)): A sum *per root mass*, denoted by $(\cdot)_\#$, begins without specified old labels.
- **Scalar response and reference defect** ([source](#pm-h-13)): Below put $$q(v)=\Gamma(K(v)),\qquad h_*(v)=K(v)-b(v)q(v),\qquad d(v)=h(v)-h_*(v).$$
- **Centered log Laplace transform** ([source](#eq:A4)): The mass-$s$ power mean then gives $${\cal K}_m(s)=s\,m\psi_m(s)=\log\mathbf E\exp\{s(G_m-\mathbf E G_m)\}, \tag{A4}\label{eq:A4}$$ where $G_m$ is the random total continuation just after the initial matrix revelation in the untilted path.
- **Finite jet** ([source](#eq:A5)): A *jet* means that the series is retained only through a specified finite degree; no convergence of an infinite series is being asserted.
- **Common finite pressure symbol** ([source](#eq:A6)): The clock derivative and the coefficient linear in the number of added sites will be expressed through the same pressure symbol, namely $${\cal I}=\log\Psi_K(J)-\tfrac14\sum b_{ij}(Q^*_{ij})^2 . \tag{A6}\label{eq:A6}$$
- **Resolution sheet** ([source](#sec:inverse)): A *sheet* $r$ consists of pairs in the same block at cut $p_r$ and different child blocks at cut $p_{r+1}$; write $K_r$ for their common scalar time.
- **Row-zero pair array** ([source](#pm-h-34)): Subtracting this projection leaves an array whose row sum on each sheet is zero. We call this the *row-zero* part.
