<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-source-calculus** [claim](#stmt-found-estimates) / [proof](#proof-stmt-found-estimates): Normalize terminal mass, use source Hessians and pinned driver inequalities, then remove the pin by zero-field gauge symmetry. -> Pressure, moment, and projection estimates.
- **step-cavity-quotient** [claim](#stmt-found-cavity-quotient) / [proof](#proof-stmt-found-cavity-quotient): Delete a site and interpolate its row to an independent scalar reference. -> Finite quotient and insertion remainder.
- **step-reference-change** [claim](#stmt-found-reference-change) / [proof](#proof-stmt-found-reference-change): Recombine scalar covariance insertions at consistent total degree. -> Reference-change rule.
- **step-row-derivative** [claim](#stmt-found-row-derivative) / [proof](#proof-stmt-found-row-derivative): Differentiate the symbolic pressure and cancel quotient and quadratic terms. -> Pressure derivative represented by the shared symbol.
- **step-site-increment** [claim](#stmt-found-size-increment) / [proof](#proof-stmt-found-size-increment): Interpolate appended scalar rows and extract the coefficient linear in added sites. -> Finite site polynomial with total-pressure remainder.
- **step-base-profile** [claim](#stmt-paths-base-profile) / [proof](#proof-stmt-paths-base-profile): Use scalar stationarity, full support, and annealed endpoint curvature. -> Regular active profile and strict top plateau.
- **step-scalar-lift** [claim](#stmt-paths-lift) / [proof](#proof-stmt-paths-lift): Perturb initial density and compare scalar PDEs and coupled diffusions. -> Quantitative response gap.
- **step-parameter-regularity** [claim](#stmt-paths-parameter-regularity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-paths-parameter-regularity): Differentiate inverse profiles and terminal data; integrate after cancelling inverse density factors. -> Local derivative cancellation and integrated size regularity.
- **step-path-switch** [claim](#stmt-paths-switch) / [proof](#proof-stmt-paths-switch): Extend the hard path by a large field jump and compare clock integrals. -> Small regularization-switch cost.
- **step-sector-response** [claim](#stmt-inv-sector-response) / [proof](#proof-stmt-inv-sector-response-2): Use conditional independence for row-zero arrays and colored covariance variations for additive arrays. -> Positive Hessian kernels and mass-weighted differences.
- **step-pair-inverse** [claim](#stmt-inv-pair-inverse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-inv-sector-response): Invert each sector and combine block projections by Abel summation before taking absolute values. -> Inverse with uniform absolute attachment domination.
- **step-residual-blocks** [claim](#stmt-global-residual-blocks) / [proof](#proof-stmt-global-residual-blocks): Block future martingale increments and integrate translated disjoint grids. -> Residual and integrated increment bounds.
- **step-buffer-brackets** [claim](#stmt-global-buffer-brackets) / [proof](#proof-stmt-global-buffer-brackets): Bracket posterior norms by conditional earlier and later averages. -> Cut-level norm and common-past increment control.
- **step-global-trial** [claim](#stmt-global-trial-gap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-global-trial-gap): Combine scalar coercivity, constrained interpolation, rough concentration, and centered inverse absorption. -> Strict global trial-gap saving.
- **step-optimizer-geometry** [claim](#stmt-bud-geometry) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-geometry): Take first variations inside the prescribed density box. -> Cap, floor, and contact geometry.
- **step-outer-moments** [claim](#stmt-bud-outer-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-outer-moments): Close a finite raw-moment bootstrap using weighted residual layers. -> Uniform conditional raw and projection bounds.
- **step-enhanced-floor** [claim](#stmt-bud-outer-second) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-outer-second): Combine whole-cap estimates with separate sliding radius windows on the added floor. -> Dyadic second moments with an explicit enhanced-floor contribution.
- **step-common-star** [claim](#stmt-bud-common-star) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-common-star): Select a nonfloor cut from deterministic second moments, then prove all required moments at that same cut. -> Common calibration cut and separate mass and radius controls.
- **step-modified-closure** [claim](#stmt-bud-modified-closure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-modified-closure): Verify replacement analytic inputs and run finite scalar-row calibration before returning to target scale. -> Uniform target modulus and integrated coarse closure.
- **step-coarse-profile** [claim](#stmt-bud-coarse-profile) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-modified-closure-2): Exclude weak-removal violations by feasible child barriers and strong-removal violations by scalar profile curvature. -> Unconditional comparability and calibrated initial slope.
- **step-stage-envelope** [claim](#stmt-bud-envelope) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-envelope): Spread a controlled fraction of the preceding radius law, then differentiate the minimum at common differentiability points. -> Stage cost and one measurable norm majorant for every minimizer.
- **step-buffer-curvature** [claim](#stmt-bud-curvature) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-curvature): Compare scalar drifts after the weighted inverse-transport estimate. -> Curvature identity for inverse-profile discrepancy.
- **step-box-moments** [claim](#stmt-bud-box-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-box-moments): Iterate nested-buffer moment bounds and apply separate radius and mass sliding estimates. -> Moving-box moments, variance savings, and alias control.
- **step-free-forks** [claim](#stmt-bud-free-forks) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-free-forks): Sum regular dyads and slice broad caps while retaining their trace cost. -> Integrated free-fork errors.
- **step-power-margins** [claim](#stmt-bud-power-margins) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-power-margins): Check piecewise exponent extrema and the dependence on the unbounded parameter majorant. -> Strict margins for remainder absorption.
- **step-high-primitives** [claim](#stmt-bud-high-primitive) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-high-primitive): Balance auxiliary-removal and actual-field estimates, treating plateau multipliers separately. -> High projection costs and small centered primitives.
- **step-buffered-closure** [claim](#stmt-bud-closure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-closure): Expand the cavity quotient, retain fixed marginals for moving forks, and sum pinned coefficients before bounding them. -> Removal-relative buffered row closure.
- **step-profile-strengthening** [claim](#stmt-bud-strengthening) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-closure-2): Rule out buffered violations by rescaled potential energy estimates and support-gap contradictions. -> Finite-stage accuracy for all optimizers outside a common null set.
- **step-weighted-budgets** [claim](#stmt-bud-targets) / [proof](#proof-stmt-bud-closure-3): Convert final inverse-profile accuracy into local pressure comparisons and combine with the global parameter comparison. -> Genuine-path dyadic and size-path budgets.
- **step-widths** [claim](#stmt-lem-statistics-widths) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-statistics-widths): Combine intrinsic widths, deviation cones, endpoint functions, and plateau coordinates. -> Measurable deterministic windows and envelope tiles.
- **step-pointwise-moments** [claim](#stmt-prop-statistics-pointwise) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-statistics-widths-2): Close raw and refined moment bootstraps using normalized-anchor projections and two-sided brackets. -> Raw and envelope-controlled genuine-path moments.
- **step-integrated-variances** [claim](#stmt-lem-statistics-integrated) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-statistics-integrated): Integrate the source inequality tilewise, telescope past anchors, and use mass averaging. -> Weighted residual and integrated variance estimates.
- **step-localization** [claim](#stmt-lem-statistics-localized) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-statistics-localized): Retain large-envelope tiles and balance window variance against local accuracy. -> Localized direct-path variance bound.
- **step-lower-band** [claim](#stmt-lem-statistics-lower-band) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-statistics-lower-band): Use the lower field slope and balance raw bounds with mass slides. -> Residual and variance integrals above the mask.
- **step-centered-polynomials** [claim](#stmt-lem-statistics-centered) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-statistics-centered): Apply the polynomial pinned inequality after finite-moment truncation. -> Centered polynomial integral bounds.
- **step-low-projection** [claim](#stmt-cor-statistics-low-projection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-statistics-low-projection): Telescope future doubled layers with a full field gap after separation. -> Common-low-cut projection estimate.
- **step-coarse-switch** [claim](#stmt-lem-statistics-coarse-switch) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-statistics-coarse-switch): Average the large-scale event by parameter moments and integrate the multiplier singularity. -> Power-saving coarse and multiplier contributions.
- **step-size-accuracy** [claim](#stmt-prop-statistics-size-accuracy) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-statistics-size-accuracy): Freeze the long tail, vary reciprocal masses convexly, then upgrade integrated means through scalar stability and brackets. -> Uniform fixed-order moment accuracy independent of later strength choices.
- **step-low-cap** [claim](#stmt-cor-statistics-cap) / [proof](#stmt-cor-statistics-cap): Compare the uniform mean-error bound with the capped dyadic budget. -> Deterministically capped low scale with preserved parameter moment.
- **step-low-sources** [claim](#stmt-lem-statistics-low-sources) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-statistics-low-sources): Remove aliases and process stochastic vertices in decreasing time under explicitly fixed retained marginal laws. -> Centered low sources retaining the prescribed pair second norm.
- **step-high-statistics** [claim](#stmt-prop-statistics-high) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rem-statistics-earlier-pair): Invert the centered high covariance equation, absorb nonlinear terms, and solve the longitudinal mean equation. -> High-mass variance and mean savings.
- **step-centered-allocation** [claim](#stmt-exp-lem-centered-count) / [proof](#proof-stmt-exp-lem-centered-count): Classify factor multiplicities and combine envelope budgets with centered integration under a fixed marginal. -> Averaged centered allocation saving.
- **step-scalar-compression** [claim](#stmt-exp-prop-low-coefficients) / [proof](#proof-stmt-exp-prop-low-coefficients): Sum internal source placements on fixed skeletons, differentiate coefficients, and cancel leading scalar jets against size rescaling and the square correction. -> Low-degree coefficient majorants.
- **step-increment-completion** [claim](#stmt-prop-increment) / [proof](#sec:parameters): Choose size degrees before strength exponents, combine high-mass and compressed low-mass bounds, and retain a common integrable envelope for moving site weights. -> Stopped increment estimate with a common strict saving.
- **step-augmentation** [claim](#stmt-red-lem-augmentation) / [proof](#proof-stmt-red-lem-augmentation): Telescope pinned transition densities and marginalize a convex epigraph after exponential augmentation. -> Log-concavity and stopped density moments.
- **step-site-smoothing** [claim](#stmt-red-lem-site-smoothing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-red-lem-site-smoothing): Transfer the stencil to smooth weights and interpolate one added spin. -> Site smoothing and neighboring-transform errors.
- **step-dyadic-transforms** [claim](#stmt-red-prop-dyadic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-red-prop-dyadic): Follow a stopped direct-size-reverse route, average nearby sites, and exclude a first stop violation. -> Uniform transform comparison within each dyad.
- **step-moment-reduction** [claim](#stmt-red-prop-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-red-prop-moments): Interpolate positive Laplace tests, sum dyadic errors, exclude zero variance using the exponent lower bound, and remove augmentation. -> Power-rate moments and a moment-determinate full-sequence limit.
- **step-moment-theorem** [claim](#stmt-thm-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-red-prop-moments): Apply the completed increment deduction and enlarge constants over remaining finite sizes. -> Quantitative moment theorem and uniform exponential integrability.
- **step-law-identification** [claim](#stmt-red-prop-identification) / [proof](#proof-stmt-red-prop-identification): Continue the moment Dirichlet series across its boundary, evaluate its Taylor expansion after expectation, and randomize a replicated coefficient. -> Absolutely convergent moment specification and integrable finite experiment.
- **step-moment-specification** [claim](#stmt-def-law) / [proof](#proof-stmt-red-prop-identification): Average comparison copies conditionally and apply the identified expectation series. -> Finite-system specification of the limiting standardized moments.
- **step-main-law** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#proof-stmt-red-prop-moments): Remove the independent Gaussian completion and standardize by the exact finite-size variance. -> Nondegenerate standardized full-sequence limiting law.
- **step-curie-weiss** [claim](#stmt-cor-skcw) / [proof](#proof-stmt-exp-prop-low-coefficients-2): Integrate the perturbation tail bound and compare exact standard deviations in the coupled models. -> Perturbed variance asymptotic and standardized law.
- **step-chaos** [claim](#stmt-cor-disorder-chaos) / [proof](#proof-stmt-exp-prop-low-coefficients-3): Apply Gaussian variance and coordinate-replacement inequalities with explicit covariance normalization. -> Sufficient annealed disorder-chaos scales.

Every derivative order and compact time interval is fixed before $N\\to\\infty$.*\n\n*For the direct reference, the normalized inverse near zero has uniformly bounded one-sided derivatives of every fixed order. Their $\\log\\lambda$ derivatives are $O(\\lambda)$, and $$\\partial_{\\log\\lambda}q(v)=O(\\lambda\\min(v,1)).$$ At fixed sufficiently small normalized time $\\xi$, the $\\log\\lambda$ derivative of $1-\\widehat\\Gamma'(\\xi)/\\widehat\\Gamma'(0)$ is $O(\\lambda\\xi^2)$.*\n\n\n*For the smoothed reference, write $\\widehat V_j$ and $\\widehat\\Gamma_j$ to display the terminal mass $j=4/\\ell$. On each fixed compact scalar-time interval $[0,R]$, and for every fixed spatial order $r\\ge1$, there are constants $C_r,c_r>0$ such that $$\\sup_{0\\le\\xi\\le R,\\ z\\in\\mathbb R}\n \\left|\\partial_j\\partial_z^r\\widehat V_j(\\xi,z)\\right|\n \\le C_r e^{-c_rM}.$$ For a fixed sufficiently small $\\xi_0>0$, this implies the more precise cancellation $$\\left|\\partial_j\\bigl(\n       \\widehat\\Gamma'_j(\\xi)-\\widehat\\Gamma'_j(0)\\bigr)\\right|\n \\le C e^{-cM}\\xi^2,\n \\qquad 0\\le\\xi\\le\\xi_0.                              \\tag{P2a}\\label{eq:P2a}$$ For a fixed sufficiently small mass $v_0>0$, the smoothed reference also satisfies, for each fixed $r\\ge0$, $$\\sup_{0\\le v\\le v_0}\n \\bigl(|\\partial_v^r t|+|\\partial_v^r q|\n       +|\\partial_\\theta\\partial_v^r t|\n       +|\\partial_\\theta\\partial_v^r q|\\bigr)\\le C_r,$$ with one-sided derivatives at zero. The physical initial spatial derivatives obey the rescaling bound, for each fixed $r\\ge1$, $$\\left|\\partial_\\theta\\left(\n     \\ell^{1-r}\\partial_z^r V(0,0)\\right)\\right|\n \\le C_r e^{-c_rM}.$$*\n\n*Over the full mass interval $(0,4)$, the smoothed clocks $t,q$ are absolutely continuous in $\\theta$, with $$\\int_0^4\\bigl(|\\partial_\\theta t(v)|\n                  +|\\partial_\\theta q(v)|\\bigr)\\,dv\n \\le C M^C.                                            \\tag{P2b}\\label{eq:P2b}$$ The constants in this integrated bound contain no inverse power of $\\omega$.",

          "anchor": "stmt-inv-sector-response",
          "exact_quote": "Use the finite resolution above, and put $m_t=V_z(K_t,Z_{K_t})$, $\\chi_t=V_{zz}(K_t,Z_{K_t})$. Let $\\mathbf E_t$ condition on the scalar prefix through $K_t$. On the row-zero sector, different sheets do not mix. On sheet $r$, the multiplier in the child resolutions $\\widetilde E_i^r\\otimes\\widetilde E_l^r$, $i,l\\ge r+1$, is $$g_r^{il}=\\mathbf E[(\\mathbf E_r\\chi_{i-1})\n                         (\\mathbf E_r\\chi_{l-1})].$$ On the additive sector associated with $E_k$, the action on sheet coefficients is $$({\\bf M}^k f)_r=g_r^k f_r-\\sum_t B^k_{rt}\\mu_t^k f_t,\\qquad\n g_t^k=\\mathbf E[\\chi_t\\chi_{\\max(k-1,t)}].\n \\tag{H2}\\label{eq:H2}$$ Here $A=K_{k-1}$, with $A=0$ for $k=0$, and $$B^k_{rt}=\\mathbf E\\left[\n   \\operatorname{Hess}_{z,\\alpha}V(A,Z_A)[\\beta_r,\\beta_t]\\right],\n \\qquad\n \\beta_t=\\begin{cases}\n (m_t,0),&t<k,\\\\\n (0,\\delta_{K_t}),&t\\ge k.\n \\end{cases}$$ The Hessian varies the starting field and the subsequent mass profile. The prefix values $m_t$, $t<k$, are held fixed during this differentiation, and $\\delta_{K_t}$ denotes an impulse in the subsequent profile. Expectation is taken after evaluating the Hessian. The matrix $B^k$ is positive semidefinite. Restricting either action to retained levels discards the other input and output sheets.*\n\n*The kernels $B^k,g^k$ are bounded and Lipschitz in their evaluation times with polynomial constants. Their changes with the resolution index satisfy $$\\|B^{k+1}-B^k\\|_\\infty+\\|g^{k+1}-g^k\\|_\\infty\n \\lesssim_{\\rm pol}p_k(K_k-K_{k-1}).$$ A successive difference of $g_r^{il}$ in index $i$ is bounded by $Cp_i(K_i-K_{i-1})$; a mixed difference is bounded by the product of the corresponding two bounds. Moreover $0\\le g_r^k,g_r^{il}\\le\\mathbf E\\chi_r^2$. These formulas apply with arbitrary old-label topologies under the coefficient convention just described. For $k=0$, their Hessian kernel also satisfies $$|B^0_{rt}|\\lesssim C(1+K_{R+1})^C K_{\\min(r,t)}$$ when the earlier evaluation time is small.",

          "exact_quote": "The kernel <a href=\"#eq:A8\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:A8\">[eq:A8]</a> is considered on extensions of any *fixed* finite list of old labels. Indices in this section used as pair arguments are distinct leaves. Normalize terminal mass to 1; other bounded terminal masses reduce to this by mass rescaling, scaling cumulative covariances by the square of the mass. Take a monotone step scalar path $K$, nonnegative bounded-variation step multiplier $b$, and retain pair levels in a terminal interval of the hierarchy (the whole interval is allowed). Suppose at these levels $$1-b_r\\mathbf E\\chi_r^2\\ge e>0,\\qquad \\chi_r=V_{zz}(K_r,Z_{K_r}).$$ Bounds called polynomial in this section are in $1+K_{\\rm top}+\\|b\\|_\\infty+\\operatorname{var}b+e^{-1}$, independent of the number of steps. On the retained levels $$u_{ab}\\ \\longmapsto\\ u_{ab}-\\sum_{cd\\ {\\rm retained}}{\\bf M}_{ab,cd} b_{cd}u_{cd}\n                                                                     \\tag{H1}\\label{eq:H1}$$ has an inverse on each finite step resolution. Each output is an integral of inputs over allocations of up to two more labels (some arguments can also be reused), with weights dominated by a polynomial times the ordinary *absolute* unrestricted attachment rules to the old tree including $ab$. Restrictions and bounded weights can depend on the topology. This formulation in particular controls new split densities, allowing coincidences and ties to existing forks. It applies with $ab$ using old labels too. We only need symmetric arrays (on antisymmetric ones the subtracted sum is zero).",

          "anchor": "stmt-global-residual-blocks",
          "exact_quote": "Fix a positive path law with terminal mass $a\\in[1,4]$, and parametrize a deterministic increasing family of revealed cuts by $s$. At a cut $s$, let branches $\\mathsf a,\\mathsf b$ be conditionally independent continuations with their normalized positive kernels, given the common prefix. Partition their futures into the same $k$ deterministic blocks, the last ending at the terminal spin. Write $\\Delta_j$ for the martingale increments, so that $y-X_s=\\sum_{j=1}^k\\Delta_j$, and let $\\mu'_j\\le a$ be the largest mass in block $j$. Evaluating $W_s$ on branch $\\mathsf a$, we have $$W_s\\le k\\sum_{i,j}\\mu'_j\\,\n    \\mathbf E_{\\mathsf b}[(\\Delta_i^{\\mathsf a}\\cdot\\Delta_j^{\\mathsf b})^2\\mid\\mathsf a].\n \\label{eq:global-block-decomposition}$$ Conditioning on $\\mathsf a$ retains its whole branch and the common prefix; only continuation $\\mathsf b$ is averaged. For any deterministic interval $J$, any increment length $l>0$, and $q\\ge1$, provided all indicated cuts exist, put $s_-=\\inf J$ and $s_+=\\sup J+2l$. Then $$\\left\\|\\int_J|X_{s+2l}-X_{s+l}|^2ds\\right\\|_q\n       \\le C_q l\\,\\bigl\\||X_{s_+}-X_{s_-}|^2\\bigr\\|_q .\n \\label{eq:global-grid}$$ The same estimate holds with increment $X_{s+l}-X_s$. For any nonnegative process $V_s$, not necessarily adapted, $$\\left\\|\\int\\mathbf E_sV_s\\,ds\\right\\|_q\n       \\le C_q\\left\\|\\int V_s\\,ds\\right\\|_q .\n \\label{eq:global-dual-doob}$$",
          "source_id": "PM-217.1"
        }

From such a nontrivial point there is also remaining forward $z$-length at least a small fixed macroscopic constant (for taking longer layers up to a macroscopic mass), with <a href=\"#eq:D3\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:D3\">[eq:D3]</a> holding using each successive scale.*\n\n\n3.  *Partition any full band as above into consecutive tiles of lengths comparable to $\\mathfrak h$, with this width and $e$ comparable over each tile. Writing $\\mu_I=\\int_I G_z dz/r$, $$\\sup_I G_z\\lesssim b_\\epsilon^{-C}(r\\mu_I/|I|+x^K),\\quad\n     \\Delta_I S\\lesssim b_\\epsilon^{-1}\\min(r,Z^2 |I|),\\quad\n     \\sum_I \\sup_I(e/r)^2\\lesssim Z^2 .                                 \\tag{D5}\\label{eq:D5}$$ The variation assertion holds also on comparable-scale enlargements of these tiles within the path.",

          "anchor": "stmt-prop-statistics-pointwise",
          "exact_quote": "Assume the direct-path hypotheses above and $Y=o(1)$, or their low-region size-path variant. At $v\\lesssim Y$ use $r=e=Y$ in this last assertion and <a href=\"#eq:D2\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:D2\">[eq:D2]</a>.",

          "exact_quote": "Consider an allocation with bounded degree and bounded topology weights.           "anchor": "stmt-exp-lem-centered-count",
          "exact_quote": "Fix $j\\ge2$ pair factors. Each factor is either $\\delta$, possibly projected, or a deterministic function bounded by $O_\\diamond(e(v))$; use $e=Y$ on the lower band. Fix the bands, their order, and every projection cut. Each projection cut lies after the split of its pair. Let $s=1,\\ldots,l$ index the distinct vertices to which these factors are assigned, with multiplicities $k_s$ and band scales $r_s$, and put $w=\\max_s r_s$. Suppose that the deterministic weights are common to both ensembles and, on each of boundedly many topology shapes, are bounded by $$O_\\diamond(\\lambda w^{5-j})\\ \\prod_{s=1}^l dv_s/w,                    \\tag{E2}\\label{eq:E1}$$ times measures of bounded volume in the other integration variables. These are product majorants, so deterministic restrictions may be retained. If $j=l=2$, assume in addition the factor $O_\\diamond(\\min_s r_s/w)$. More explicitly, if $H$ is this deterministic weight and $T_i^{\\mathrm{tilt}},T_i^0$ are the pair factors in the two ensembles, we estimate $$\\int H\\left\\{\\nu^{\\mathrm{tilt}}\n       \\left[\\prod_{i=1}^jT_i^{\\mathrm{tilt}}\\right]\n       -\\nu^0\\left[\\prod_{i=1}^jT_i^0\\right]\\right\\}.$$ The weight, deterministic factors, cuts, and centering $S$ are common; only the positive law and the masked overlap vary. The absolute value of this difference is bounded by $$O_\\diamond\\big(\\lambda Y^5(x/Y+g_B)\\big)+O(x^K)                       \\tag{E3}\\label{eq:E2}$$ where $K$ can be arbitrarily large. Indeed the two contributions are $$\\lambda Y^5\\frac{x}{Y}=x^5\\lambda^{1-2s_*}Z^4,\n \\qquad\n \\lambda Y^5g_B=x^5\\lambda^{(1-\\eta)/2-s_*}Z^{7/2}.$$ Both powers of $\\lambda$ are positive. Since $\\mathbf E_\\gamma Z^4\\lesssim_\\circ1$, the averaged bound is $O(x^{5+c'})$ for some $c'>0$, after taking the allowed losses smaller than these gains.",

          "anchor": "stmt-exp-prop-low-coefficients",
          "exact_quote": "Fix the dyadic restrictions on the base factors and a cut $c\\gg w$ within the region where the small inverse is regular. A sufficiently large fixed separation factor is enough; on size paths require also $c\\lesssim\\lambda$. Group base slots into blocks that share their path through $c$. Their split tree below $c$ is the *skeleton*, and every designated pair joins distinct blocks.*\n\n\n*Apply the operator ${\\cal O}$ defined above to the pressure polynomial <a href=\"#eq:E3\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:E3\">[eq:E3]</a>: it is $1+\\partial_\\theta$, with the formal action $\\partial_\\theta\\Delta=-\\Delta/6$, on a size path, and $\\partial_{\\log\\lambda}$, holding $\\Delta$ fixed, on a direct path. Group the resulting signed allocation coefficients by this skeleton and sum their internal placements within each block. The bound below concerns these differentiated, grouped coefficients. This is a rearrangement of a signed measure. The probabilistic expectations used to evaluate the coefficients remain positive scalar laws on each fixed topology. The spin-model pair tests have been projected to $c$, or to a neighboring smaller cut, so they depend only on the skeleton and can be kept outside the internal sums. For $j=2,3,4$, the resulting coefficient, including the skeleton allocation weight, is bounded by $$O_\\diamond(\\lambda c^{5-j})\\prod_{s\\ {\\rm skeleton\\ fork}} dv_s/c .       \\tag{E4}\\label{eq:E4}$$ If $j=2$, the designated vertices are distinct, and $c\\asymp w$, the bound includes the further factor $O_\\diamond(\\min_s r_s/c)$. A factor $d$ or $\\dot d$ may first contribute $\\lambda c^2$ to the coefficient, leaving a deterministic factor bounded by the ordinary envelope because $r\\lesssim c$. Like $b$ and $\\dot b$, these weights are constant during each internal block sum.*\n\n*Combine contributions only when they multiply the same product of pair tests on the same skeleton. In particular, this combines a repeated pair with the square counterterm. Give such terms the same dyadic restrictions and projection cuts. The cut, shape, and mass coordinates are fixed during coefficient differentiation. Internal summation may then be done before or after that differentiation. The spin tests receive only the formal action on $\\Delta$ already specified: project the differentiated polynomial, without differentiating a random test or a projection law.",

          "anchor": "stmt-thm-moments",
          "exact_quote": "For each fixed $\\beta>1$, there are real numbers $a_k=a_k(\\beta)$, $k\\ge1$, with the following property. For every integer $k\\ge1$, there are constants $c_k>0$ and $C_k<\\infty$ such that $$\\label{eq:moment-rate}\n \\big|\\mathbb E Y_n^k-a_k\\big|\\le C_k n^{-c_k},\\qquad n\\ge2.$$ There are also constants $c>0$ and $C<\\infty$, depending on $\\beta$, for which $$\\label{eq:exponential-moments}\n \\sup_{n\\ge2}\\mathbb E e^{c|Y_n|}\\le C.$$ The limits satisfy $a_1=0$ and $0<a_2<\\infty$.",

      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-def-law",
          "exact_quote": "Fix $\\beta>1$ and let $C=\\sum_{l=2}^{\\infty}l^{-2}$. For an integer $k\\ge1$, draw an integer $J\\ge2$ with $$\\mathbb P(J=l)=\\frac{l^{-2}}C.$$ Conditional on $J$, draw $k+1$ independent copies $F_J^{c,0},\\ldots,F_J^{c,k}$ of the completed free energy in <a href=\"#eq:completed-free-energy\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:completed-free-energy\">[eq:completed-free-energy]</a>. Set $$t=\\log J,\n \\qquad P_k=\\prod_{i=1}^k J^{-1/6}(F_J^{c,0}-F_J^{c,i}).$$ Conditional averaging over the independent comparison copies gives $\\mathbb E[P_k\\mid J=l]=\\mathbb E Y_l^k$. The constants in Theorem <a href=\"#thm:moments\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:moments\">2</a> satisfy $$\\label{eq:law-moments}\n a_k=C\\sum_{h=0}^{\\infty}\n \\mathbb E\\!\\left[P_k\\left(\\frac{t^h}{h!}\n       -\\mathbf1_{\\{h\\ge1\\}}\\frac{t^{h-1}}{(h-1)!}\\right)\\right],$$ where the second term is absent for $h=0$. <a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-fixed-temperature-limit**: The exactly centered and standardized zero-field Gaussian Ising free energy converges along all integer sizes to a nondegenerate law with mean zero, variance one, and an exponential moment near the origin.
- **invariant-completed-moment-convergence**: Every fixed positive integer moment of the centered completed free energy converges at a positive power rate. The limiting second moment is finite and strictly positive, and exponential moments are uniformly bounded near the origin.
- **invariant-average-before-summation**: The finite-system characterization recovers limiting moments by summing scalar expectations. Absolute convergence applies after taking those expectations; the unaveraged pointwise series cannot be interchanged with expectation.
- **invariant-normalized-future-kernels**: Projection bounds require the projected branch to retain its normalized future kernel conditional on its prefix and exterior data. A centered integral with a moving fork requires a fixed marginal law before applying unconditional inequalities to retained random factors.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-use-varying-temperature**: Apply the limiting law to temperatures approaching the transition or to an arbitrary temperature schedule. -> The fixed-temperature theorem supplies no uniform conclusion for such a schedule.
- **anti-use-external-field-or-other-disorder**: Transfer the variance asymptotic to an externally biased model or replace the Gaussian couplings without further proof. -> The model assumptions and the zero-field identities used in the argument no longer establish the asserted conclusion.
- **anti-use-pointwise-series**: Sum the random Taylor terms pointwise and then average the resulting sum to estimate the limiting moments. -> The pointwise cancellation fails to recover the positive limiting second moment.
- **anti-use-conditioning-on-future**: Condition a projection estimate on an observation from the affected future branch, or use retained random factors as deterministic weights. -> The required conditional future kernel or deterministic-weight hypothesis can fail, invalidating the projection or centered moment estimate.
- **anti-use-sharp-chaos-threshold**: Interpret the disorder-chaos estimates as a sharp transition, a quenched guarantee, or an overlap result for the ferromagnetically perturbed model. -> The source proves sufficient annealed perturbation scales for the original zero-field model only.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The principal results concern convergence over unbounded system sizes, limiting moments, and an infinite expectation-first series. A finite collection of evaluations cannot decide these assertions. The randomized moment representation is almost surely finite but has unbounded sampled sizes and replication levels; the source explicitly states: “Here the levels index Taylor coefficients; the integrability and almost-sure finiteness proved below do not assert finite expected work or import the SDE complexity guarantees of that reference.” This construction does not supply a bounded finite oracle for the limiting law or its moments.

## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-fixed-temperature** (hypothesis): The fluctuation conclusions require a fixed inverse temperature above the transition; they provide no uniform varying-temperature limit. Blocked use: ['Apply the limiting law to a temperature approaching the transition.', 'Exchange the temperature limit with the system-size limit.']
- **limit-model-and-field** (hypothesis): The model uses independent standard Gaussian pair couplings, Ising configurations, the displayed interaction normalization, and no external field. Extensions to other disorder, interaction geometry, or spins are not established here. Blocked use: ['Transfer the variance asymptotic to sparse interactions or non-Gaussian disorder without an extension.', 'Apply zero-field identities to an externally biased model.']
- **limit-exact-standardization** (hypothesis): The standardized limiting law uses the exact finite-size expectation and variance. Blocked use: ['Replace finite-size centering by a thermodynamic mean without bounding the centering error.', 'Treat an asymptotic variance estimate as an exact finite-size normalization.']
- **limit-law-identification** (unknown): The source specifies the limiting law through its moments and does not identify a named distribution or prove that it is non-Gaussian. Blocked use: ['Label the limiting law Gaussian or non-Gaussian solely from nondegeneracy.', 'Substitute a named distribution for the specified moment law.']
- **limit-expectation-before-series** (formal_scope): Absolute convergence is asserted for the series of scalar expectations after averaging, not for an interchange of expectation with the unaveraged pointwise series. Blocked use: ['Sum the random Taylor terms pointwise before averaging.', 'Use pointwise cancellation to conclude that the limiting second moment vanishes.']
- **limit-randomized-work** (formal_scope): The randomized moment representation is integrable and almost surely finite, but finite expected work and computational complexity guarantees are not asserted. Blocked use: ['Advertise the representation as an efficient sampler for the limiting law.', 'Infer finite expected computational work from almost-sure termination.']
- **limit-pinned-polynomial-scope** (hypothesis): Pinned moment estimates require zero deterministic external field, deterministic weights and polynomial coefficients, and the full single-path law. Blocked use: ['Insert a retained random branch factor as a deterministic weight.', 'Apply the pinned estimate under arbitrary conditioning.']
- **limit-projection-kernel** (hypothesis): Projection requires a positive traversed field interval after separation from the anchor data, a positive lower mass, the stated clock bounds, and preservation of the branch's normalized conditional future law. Blocked use: ['Condition on an observation from the future being projected.', 'Invoke the projection estimate without its field-length and mass lower bounds.']
- **limit-signed-allocation** (formal_scope): Signed attachment coefficients are not probabilities. Row collapse requires attachment-independent summands, and cancellations must precede absolute estimates. Blocked use: ['Sample signed attachment weights as a probability distribution.', 'Collapse a row whose test depends on the detailed attachment.', 'Discard fork atoms before performing signed cancellations.']
- **limit-finite-expansion-order** (approximation): The cavity, row, and site expansions retain fixed finite Taylor orders with controlled remainders. They do not assert convergence of infinite replica expansions. Blocked use: ['Discard insertion or row-deletion remainders.', 'Interpret the finite jets as analytic continuation in replica count.', 'Multiply the total-pressure site remainder by an additional site-count factor.']
- **limit-admissible-path-construction** (hypothesis): Reference changes and covariance interpolations require monotone references and admissible positive covariance paths; the size increment also requires the stated monotonicity of the matrix-reference product. Blocked use: ['Apply the quotient along a covariance interpolation that loses positivity.', 'Use the site-increment identity without its monotonicity assumption.', 'Differentiate sampled overlaps instead of the formal polynomial.']
- **limit-stopped-transfer** (hypothesis): The high-accuracy derivative and tilted-density transfers are used on the stated deterministic Laplace stop; they are not unconditional estimates outside that set. Blocked use: ['Use stopped density moment bounds after removing the stopping condition.', 'Treat independent active forest components as sharing an untilted root.']
- **limit-inverse-strict-gap** (hypothesis): The pair inverse requires its strict retained-level scalar gap, a monotone step scalar path, a nonnegative bounded-variation multiplier, and a fixed finite old-label topology. Its bound includes polynomial dependence on the inverse gap. Blocked use: ['Claim uniform inverse control as the gap closes.', 'Extend the estimate to an increasing number of old labels without new bounds.']
- **limit-modified-optimizer-inputs** (hypothesis): Outer moment estimates are conditional on outer regularity; the coarse modified closure additionally requires strong removal. Modified density constraints require their replacement analytic estimates before closure is used. Blocked use: ['Assume outer comparability while using its conditional estimates to prove that same comparability.', "Apply the companion's original optimization hypotheses directly to the modified density box."]
- **limit-optimizer-and-window-selection** (hypothesis): Optimizer majorants hold outside a common exceptional parameter set. Calibration cuts and averaging windows are selected from deterministic path data before sampling spins. Blocked use: ['Select a favorable buffer after inspecting a spin realization.', 'Replace an almost-everywhere common-majorant statement by an assertion at every parameter.']
- **limit-fixed-marginal-centered-integration** (hypothesis): Centered integration over a moving fork requires an explicitly retained marginal law independent of that moving coordinate. The centered inequality is unconditional before other random tests are handled. Blocked use: ["Apply a centered path inequality while the retained test's law changes with the fork.", 'Condition the centered inequality on the retained random pair.']
- **limit-fixed-size-path-limits** (formal_scope): Path approximation is taken at each fixed system size with prescribed observations and jump fillings preserved. No approximation rate uniform in system size is inferred. Blocked use: ['Replace the fixed-size limiting argument by an unspecified size-uniform discretization rate.', 'Change the joint filling at an observed intermediate jump.']
- **limit-compression-and-parameter-order** (hypothesis): Low-degree compression combines only coefficients multiplying the same projected tests on the same skeleton. Cuts remain fixed during differentiation, and finite orders and exponent choices precede the size limit. Blocked use: ['Differentiate a moving projection law as part of the formal coefficient operator.', 'Combine counterterms with differently restricted pair tests.', 'Choose expansion orders after taking the size limit.']
- **limit-curie-weiss-coupling** (hypothesis): The ferromagnetic comparison is confined to the displayed fixed coupling regime below unit coupling. Blocked use: ['Apply the invariance corollary at unit coupling.', 'Use the corollary for a coupling varying with system size.']
- **limit-chaos-conclusion** (formal_scope): The disorder-chaos scales are sufficient annealed bounds for the original model. They do not establish sharpness, quenched decorrelation, or an overlap conclusion for the ferromagnetic extension. Blocked use: ['Interpret the sufficient scales as a sharp transition.', 'Transfer the overlap statement to the SK–Curie–Weiss model.', 'Treat Gibbs overlap bounds as guarantees for a ground-state solver.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


For every fixed inverse temperature <i>β</i> &gt; 1, we prove that the zero-field Gaussian Ising Sherrington–Kirkpatrick free energy, centered by its expectation and divided by its standard deviation, converges in distribution to a nondegenerate law as the system size tends to infinity through all integers. We also prove that its variance divided by <i>n</i><sup>1/3</sup> converges to a finite positive constant.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

At a fixed temperature below the transition, how large are the sample-to-sample fluctuations of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick free energy, and do they approach a law after centering and rescaling? We prove a limiting law for every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>1$ in the zero-field Gaussian Ising model. The result includes a positive variance prefactor at scale $n^{1/3}$ and a characterization of the law by finite-system moments.

<a id="eq:model"></a>
Let $(g_{ij})_{1\le i<j\le n}$ be independent standard Gaussian variables. For $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n$ and $\beta>1$, put $$\label{eq:model}
 H_n(\sigma)=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i<j}g_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j,
 \qquad Z_n(\beta)=\sum_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n}e^{\beta H_n(\sigma)},
 \qquad F_n(\beta)=\log Z_n(\beta).$$ All expectations concern the Gaussian disorder unless another probability law is explicitly specified. There is no external field. Write $$s_n(\beta)^2=\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}F_n(\beta),
 \qquad X_n(\beta)=\frac{F_n(\beta)-\mathbb E F_n(\beta)}{s_n(\beta)}.$$ The variance is positive for every $n\ge2$: with all couplings except $g_{12}$ set to zero, the free energy is $n\log2+\log\cosh(\beta g_{12}/\sqrt n)$, a nonconstant continuous function. Full support of the Gaussian law excludes almost-sure constancy. Standard Gaussian moment bounds give finite variance.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### The fluctuation problem and its history

The model <a href="#eq:model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:model">[eq:model]</a> was introduced by Sherrington and Kirkpatrick (Sherrington and Kirkpatrick 1975) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[SK1975](#ref-SK1975)]. Their symmetric replica calculation gave an unphysical negative entropy at zero temperature. Parisi’s hierarchy (Parisi 1979) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[Parisi1979](#ref-Parisi1979)] replaced a single overlap parameter by successive levels, encoded in the infinite-level limit by a function. This development led to a variational formula for the thermodynamic free energy. Gaussian interpolation established the thermodynamic limit (Guerra and Toninelli 2002) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[GuerraToninelli2002](#ref-GuerraToninelli2002)], the variational bound of Guerra (Guerra 2003) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Guerra2003](#ref-Guerra2003)], and ultimately the matching formula proved by Talagrand (Talagrand 2006) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[Talagrand2006](#ref-Talagrand2006)]. Panchenko’s extension treats general mixed $p$-spin models, including odd interactions (Panchenko 2014) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[Panchenko2014](#ref-Panchenko2014)]. These results identify the leading order of the mean free energy. They leave the smaller, sample-dependent fluctuations studied here.

The one-sixth fluctuation prediction has a separate physics history. Kondor’s replica expansion (Kondor 1983) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[Kondor1983](#ref-Kondor1983)] and the finite-size prediction of Crisanti, Paladin, Sommers, and Vulpiani (Crisanti et al. 1992) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[CPSV1992](#ref-CPSV1992)] preceded the low-temperature large-deviation calculations of Parisi and Rizzo (Parisi and Rizzo 2008, 2009) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[ParisiRizzo2008](#ref-ParisiRizzo2008), [ParisiRizzo2009](#ref-ParisiRizzo2009)]. The predicted $n^{-5/6}$ scale for the physical free-energy density becomes $n^{1/6}$ for $\log Z_n$ at fixed $\beta$. To pass from rare free energies to the width of typical fluctuations, Parisi and Rizzo assume that the large-deviation tail matches smoothly onto the central part of the distribution (Parisi and Rizzo 2009, sec. VI) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[ParisiRizzo2009](#ref-ParisiRizzo2009)]. They distinguish the two orders of the replica-number and system-size limits. This matching argument is heuristic: it does not itself provide a variance asymptotic or a limiting law.

Rigorous fluctuation results depend strongly on the regime. Aizenman, Lebowitz, and Ruelle proved order-one Gaussian fluctuations at high temperature (Aizenman, Lebowitz, and Ruelle 1987) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[AizenmanLebowitzRuelle1987](#ref-AizenmanLebowitzRuelle1987)]. Chatterjee obtained superconcentration and its relation to disorder chaos (Chatterjee 2009) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[Chatterjee2009](#ref-Chatterjee2009)], as well as a constant-scale nonconcentration bound (Chatterjee 2019) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[Chatterjee2019LowerBounds](#ref-Chatterjee2019LowerBounds)]. Chen and Lam’s critical and near-critical bounds concern temperatures approaching the transition (Chen and Lam 2019) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[ChenLam2019Critical](#ref-ChenLam2019Critical)]. For each fixed $\beta>1$, Aronow and Lopatto prove $$c_\beta n^{4/15}\le \mathop{\mathrm{Var}}F_n(\beta)\le C_\beta n^{7/15}$$ in (Aronow and Lopatto 2026, Theorem 1.4) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[AL2026](#ref-AL2026)], and quantitative tail estimates in a separate deviation window in (Aronow and Lopatto 2026, Theorem 1.5) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[AL2026](#ref-AL2026)]. These bounds allow, but do not establish, variance of order $n^{1/3}$. Recent critical-window limits (Cheng et al. 2026, Theorem 2.1) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[ChengLiuShaoXu2026CriticalWindow](#ref-ChengLiuShaoXu2026CriticalWindow)] concern $\beta_n\to1$, while the all-temperature results of Chen, Dey, and Panchenko require a nonzero field (Chen, Dey, and Panchenko 2017) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[ChenDeyPanchenko2017](#ref-ChenDeyPanchenko2017)]. Neither hypothesis covers the fixed zero-field model here.

Our companion *The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick fluctuation scale* (OpenAI 2026) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[PE](#ref-PE)], abbreviated *PE*, supplies both its finite-tree comparison toolkit and the fixed-temperature exponent <a id="eq:PE-exponent"></a>$$\label{eq:PE-exponent}
 s_n(\beta)=n^{1/6+o(1)}.$$ The exponent alone does not identify a limiting distribution or prove convergence of the variance divided by $n^{1/3}$. The additional work here is a quantitative comparison of different sizes, with a summable error. Appendix <a href="#sec:companion-interface" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:companion-interface">12</a> lists the precise PE inputs and their hypotheses.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### The limiting law

<a id="stmt-thm-main"></a>
<div id="thm:main" class="theorem">

**Theorem 1** (Limiting law). *For every fixed real $\beta>1$, there is a nondegenerate Borel probability measure $\nu_\beta$ such that $$X_n(\beta)\ \Longrightarrow\ \nu_\beta
 \qquad\text{as }n\to\infty\text{ through all integers}.$$ The measure $\nu_\beta$ has mean zero, variance one, and a finite exponential moment in a neighborhood of the origin. It is the unique probability measure with the moments specified in Proposition <a href="#def:law" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:law">3</a> below.*

</div>

The centering and variance are the exact finite-size quantities. The formula below specifies the moments of $\nu_\beta$; no identification with a named distribution is made. The quantitative statement below proves that the variance has a positive limiting prefactor and provides the rate needed for the moment characterization.

<a id="eq:completed-free-energy"></a>
For the quantitative result, we use a Gaussian completion convenient for interpolation. Let $\zeta_n$ be a centered Gaussian of variance $\beta^2/2$, independent of the couplings, and define $$\label{eq:completed-free-energy}
 F_n^c=F_n(\beta)-n\log2+\zeta_n,
 \qquad Y_n=n^{-1/6}(F_n^c-\mathbb E F_n^c).$$ Different copies below include independent couplings and independent completion variables. The subtraction of $n\log2$ changes the counting spin prior into the uniform probability prior. The completion changes the covariance into the homogeneous quadratic-overlap covariance used later.

<a id="stmt-thm-moments"></a>
<div id="thm:moments" class="theorem">

**Theorem 2** (Moment convergence at the fluctuation scale). *For each fixed $\beta>1$, there are real numbers $a_k=a_k(\beta)$, $k\ge1$, with the following property. For every integer $k\ge1$, there are constants $c_k>0$ and $C_k<\infty$ such that <a id="eq:moment-rate"></a>$$\label{eq:moment-rate}
 \big|\mathbb E Y_n^k-a_k\big|\le C_k n^{-c_k},\qquad n\ge2.$$ There are also constants $c>0$ and $C<\infty$, depending on $\beta$, for which <a id="eq:exponential-moments"></a>$$\label{eq:exponential-moments}
 \sup_{n\ge2}\mathbb E e^{c|Y_n|}\le C.$$ The limits satisfy $a_1=0$ and $0<a_2<\infty$.*

</div>

Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a> follows from Theorem <a href="#thm:moments" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:moments">2</a> by moment determinacy and removal of the completion. Indeed, $$n^{-1/3}\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}F_n(\beta)
 =\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}Y_n-\frac{\beta^2}{2n^{1/3}}\longrightarrow a_2>0,$$ and the centered completion vanishes in $L^2$ after multiplication by $n^{-1/6}$. The exact finite-size standardization is then justified by Slutsky’s theorem. We give the complete deduction, including nondegeneracy, in Section <a href="#sec:reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:reduction">4</a>. For the physical total free energy $-\beta^{-1}F_n$, the variance constant is $a_2/\beta^2$ and its standardized limit is the reflection of $\nu_\beta$. For its density $-(\beta n)^{-1}F_n$, the variance is asymptotic to $(a_2/\beta^2)n^{-5/3}$.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
#### A finite-system characterization of the law

The power rate in Theorem <a href="#thm:moments" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:moments">2</a> allows each limiting moment to be recovered from a convergent series of finite-size averages. The following random-size experiment expresses this characterization using independent copies of the finite SK model.

<a id="stmt-def-law"></a>
<div id="def:law" class="proposition">

<a id="eq:law-moments"></a>
**Proposition 3** (Moment specification). *Fix $\beta>1$ and let $C=\sum_{l=2}^{\infty}l^{-2}$. For an integer $k\ge1$, draw an integer $J\ge2$ with $$\mathbb P(J=l)=\frac{l^{-2}}C.$$ Conditional on $J$, draw $k+1$ independent copies $F_J^{c,0},\ldots,F_J^{c,k}$ of the completed free energy in <a href="#eq:completed-free-energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:completed-free-energy">[eq:completed-free-energy]</a>. Set $$t=\log J,
 \qquad P_k=\prod_{i=1}^k J^{-1/6}(F_J^{c,0}-F_J^{c,i}).$$ Conditional averaging over the independent comparison copies gives $\mathbb E[P_k\mid J=l]=\mathbb E Y_l^k$. The constants in Theorem <a href="#thm:moments" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:moments">2</a> satisfy $$\label{eq:law-moments}
 a_k=C\sum_{h=0}^{\infty}
 \mathbb E\!\left[P_k\left(\frac{t^h}{h!}
       -\mathbf1_{\{h\ge1\}}\frac{t^{h-1}}{(h-1)!}\right)\right],$$ where the second term is absent for $h=0$. Each expectation is taken before the series is summed. The series of these scalar expectations is absolutely convergent. We have $a_2>0$, and the law in Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a> is uniquely determined by $$\int z^k\,\nu_\beta(dz)=\frac{a_k}{a_2^{k/2}},\qquad k\ge1.$$*

</div>

Section <a href="#sec:reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:reduction">4</a> proves the formula and its absolute convergence from the moment rate in Theorem <a href="#thm:moments" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:moments">2</a>.

This characterization involves only a fixed prior on finite system sizes and finite Gaussian experiments. It does not require the choice of a subsequence or knowledge of an asymptotic variance. The order in <a href="#eq:law-moments" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:law-moments">[eq:law-moments]</a> is essential: it is not permissible to interchange the unaveraged pointwise series with expectation. Section <a href="#sec:reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:reduction">4</a> also realizes each $a_k$ as the expectation of a single integrable random variable obtained from an almost surely finite experiment.

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
#### The size comparison and its main ingredients

The new estimate compares centered log Laplace transforms at different system sizes with a summable error. For a large dyadic size $N$, put $x=N^{-1/6}$. The comparison gives, for every integer $N'\in[N,2N]$, $$\left|\log\mathbb E e^{q x^\varepsilon Y_{N'}}
       -\log\mathbb E e^{q x^\varepsilon Y_N}\right|
 \le C_q x^{\varepsilon+c'},$$ where $c'>0$, $q>0$ is fixed, and $\varepsilon>0$ is sufficiently small and fixed. The saving $c'$ is independent of sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. Estimates for positive Laplace tests, together with preliminary exponential-tail bounds, recover comparisons of each fixed moment. Their errors can then be summed over dyadic intervals. This is the reduction proved in Section <a href="#sec:reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:reduction">4</a>.

To obtain the transform estimate, we interpolate through hierarchical Gaussian systems. At each level, a normalized transition kernel specifies the law of the next Gaussian increments; paths can share an initial history and then branch independently. Overlaps are normalized scalar products of the terminal spin configurations. The hierarchy is indexed by an averaging parameter, called mass; its matrix and field clocks record the cumulative variances along this index. A one-site scalar model built from the Parisi minimizer supplies reference overlaps along these clocks.

The scalar input has its own development. Auffinger and Chen proved structural properties of Parisi measures and uniqueness of the Parisi minimizer (Auffinger and Chen 2015a, 2015b) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[AuffingerChenProperties2015](#ref-AuffingerChenProperties2015), [AuffingerChenUniqueness2015](#ref-AuffingerChenUniqueness2015)]; Jagannath and Tobasco gave variational support conditions (Jagannath and Tobasco 2017) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[JagannathTobasco2017](#ref-JagannathTobasco2017)]. Zhou established interval support near the critical temperature (Zhou 2025) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[Zhou2025](#ref-Zhou2025)]. We use Lopatto’s full-support result for every fixed $\beta>1$ (Lopatto 2026, Theorem 1.1 and Lemma 2.2) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[Lopatto2026](#ref-Lopatto2026)], in the form developed in PE. The positive initial density needed here is proved in that companion from the scalar identities and full support.

The direct antecedent for our pinned-field and optimized-path comparisons is Aronow and Lopatto (Aronow and Lopatto 2026) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[AL2026](#ref-AL2026)]. Hierarchical positive laws, interpolation, and cavity calculations also have an established lineage through Ruelle’s cascade construction (Ruelle 1987) <a id="pm-cite-25"></a>[[Ruelle1987](#ref-Ruelle1987)] and the cavity variational principle of Aizenman, Sims, and Starr (Aizenman, Sims, and Starr 2003) <a id="pm-cite-26"></a>[[AizenmanSimsStarr2003](#ref-AizenmanSimsStarr2003)]. Here we work with finite normalized transition kernels and prove the quantitative larger-tree and higher-moment estimates required by the size comparison.

These comparisons use normalized probability laws. An extra future branch can be integrated out because its conditional law has mass one; conditioning on an observation from that branch can instead change the law retained in the calculation. PE’s appendix “Companion interfaces” proves the polynomial-observation bound and permits an auxiliary common temperature to vary with size; we recall these arguments when verifying their use here. The changed-constraint estimates require the additional local arguments developed in this article. Appendix <a href="#sec:companion-interface" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:companion-interface">12</a> lists the imported estimates and the hypotheses retained in their use.

Along a hierarchy we retain the initial disorder as a random input and average over the later Gaussian increments. Ordinary averaging of the resulting continuation gives one pressure; exponential averaging with a small positive parameter $s$ gives the other. Their difference, multiplied by $s$ times the number of sites, is the centered log Laplace transform. We vary the covariance clocks and take finite differences in the number of spins. Proposition <a href="#prop:increment" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:increment">15</a> bounds their combined effect with a power saving beyond the per-site scale $x^5$. With $s=q x^{1+\varepsilon}$ and $N=x^{-6}$, multiplication by $Ns$ converts this into the saving in the displayed transform estimate.

The route from $N$ to $N'$ first changes the covariance data at fixed size, then varies the size, and finally reverses the initial changes. Writing $n=N e^\theta$ and $\ell=e^{\theta/6}$ keeps the endpoint normalization equal to $n^{-1/6}$. Figure <a href="#fig:comparison-path" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:comparison-path">1</a> shows these three stages.

<figure id="fig:comparison-path">

<figcaption>The route from $N$ to an arbitrary $N′ ∈ [N,2N]$. The displayed endpoints are the centered, rescaled bare systems. The proof bounds the changes along the route and the errors from the small regularizations at its ends. One parameter vector is selected for each finite route and each Laplace test.</figcaption>
</figure>

The comparison rests on four estimates.

1.  We solve the linear equations for covariances of overlap errors. The inverse bound remains uniform when the hierarchy is refined or its masses become small. Summation by parts cancels the small-mass denominators. Contributions from branching at an already specified vertex are retained in the bound.

2.  We vary the matrix and field covariances to turn pressure comparisons into bounds on mean squared overlap errors. The constrained minimization requires estimates in both the mass coordinate and the quantile’s value. A derivative of the minimum controls every minimizer, so the argument does not need to select a minimizer measurably.

3.  We obtain higher moments for the actual comparison paths by projecting spin observations onto their revealed Gaussian histories and integrating squared martingale increments. Before integrating a centered quantity over a moving branch point, we show that the paths retained in the calculation have a law independent of that point.

4.  We sum the signed pressure coefficients before taking absolute values. Summing the scalar contributions above a fixed cut, combining the quadratic correction, and rescaling size cancel the leading terms of degrees two, three, and four. The remaining increments are summable.

<a id="pm-h-7"></a>
#### Consequences

Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a> and the variance asymptotic above instantiate the ferromagnetic comparison of Dey and Kang (Dey and Kang 2026, Proposition 1.5) <a id="pm-cite-27"></a>[[DeyKang2026](#ref-DeyKang2026)]. The comparison does not establish the zero-field law, but it gives the following consequence once that law and its positive variance prefactor are available.

<a id="stmt-cor-skcw"></a>
<div id="cor:skcw" class="corollary">

**Corollary 4** (SK–Curie–Weiss fluctuations below unit coupling). *Fix $\beta>1$ and $0\le\gamma<1$. Using the same independent standard Gaussian couplings as in <a href="#eq:model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:model">[eq:model]</a>, define the exponent and log partition function $$\begin{gathered}
 \mathcal H_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\sigma;\beta,\gamma)
 =
 \frac{\beta}{\sqrt n}\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}g_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j
 +\frac{\gamma}{2n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^n\sigma_i\right)^2,\\
 F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma)
 =\log\sum_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n}
 e^{\mathcal H_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\sigma;\beta,\gamma)}.
 \end{gathered}$$ Here $\gamma$ is the ferromagnetic coupling already in the exponent. As $n\to\infty$ through all integers, $$\begin{gathered}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Var}}F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma)
 \sim a_2(\beta)n^{1/3},\\
 \frac{F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma)
       -\mathbb E F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma)}
      {\sqrt{\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma)}}
 \Longrightarrow\nu_\beta.
 \end{gathered}$$ Here $a_2(\beta)>0$ is the constant $a_2$ above at the same $\beta$. The centering and standard deviation are the perturbed model’s own exact finite-size quantities.*

</div>

The comparison controls the added free energy in $L^2$ uniformly in $n$. Since the unperturbed standard deviation grows like $n^{1/6}$, this error disappears after either model’s exact standardization. The full argument is in Section <a href="#sec:consequences" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:consequences">11</a>.

This consequence is confined to the displayed zero-field ordered Gaussian model at fixed $\beta>1$ and $0\le\gamma<1$; it does not cover $\gamma=1$ or a coupling varying with $n$.

For the original zero-field model, the variance asymptotic also gives the following consequence of Chatterjee’s general Gaussian and replacement inequalities.

<a id="stmt-cor-disorder-chaos"></a>
<div id="cor:disorder-chaos" class="corollary">

**Corollary 5** (Upper disorder-chaos scales in zero-field SK). *Fix $\beta>1$ and $n\ge2$. Put $E_n=\{(i,j):1\le i<j\le n\}$ and $M=|E_n|=n(n-1)/2$, and let $g'$ be an independent copy of $g=(g_{ij})_{(i,j)\in E_n}$ in <a href="#eq:model" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:model">[eq:model]</a>. Write $\langle\cdot\rangle_{g,h}$ for expectation under the product of that model’s Gibbs laws with disorders $g,h$, and $R=n^{-1}\sum_i\sigma_i\tau_i$ for the overlap. Thus the replicas are independent conditional on their disorders; $\mathbb E$ below also averages the disorder and any replacement set.*

<a id="eq:chaos-ou"></a>
<a id="eq:chaos-replacement"></a>
*For $t>0$, set $g^t=e^{-t}g+\sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}\,g'$. For an integer $0\le k\le M$, let $A$ be independent of $g,g'$ and uniform over the $k$-element subsets of $E_n$. Set $g^A_{ij}=g'_{ij}$ on $A$ and $g^A_{ij}=g_{ij}$ otherwise. Then $$\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\langle R^2\rangle_{g,g^t}
 &\le \frac1n+\frac{2\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}F_n(\beta)}
                 {\beta^2n(1-e^{-t})},\label{eq:chaos-ou}\\
 \mathbb E\langle R^2\rangle_{g,g^A}
 &\le \frac1n+\frac{2(M+1)\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}F_n(\beta)}
                 {\beta^2n(k+1)}+C_\beta n^{-1/2},\label{eq:chaos-replacement}
\end{aligned}$$ for a finite constant $C_\beta$ depending only on $\beta$. As $n\to\infty$, for $t_n\ge0$ and integers $0\le k_n\le M$, these bounds imply $$\begin{aligned}
 t_n n^{2/3}\to\infty
 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathbb E\langle R^2\rangle_{g,g^{t_n}}\to0,\\
 (k_n/M)n^{2/3}\to\infty
 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathbb E\langle R^2\rangle_{g,g^{A_n}}\to0,
 \end{aligned}$$ where $A_n$ has size $k_n$ as above.*

</div>

Chatterjee’s variance identity and replacement inequality bound the mean squared overlap by the free-energy variance. Substitution of the $n^{1/3}$ variance asymptotic gives the displayed sufficient scales; Section <a href="#sec:consequences" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:consequences">11</a> checks both normalizations.

These are sufficient annealed perturbation scales, not a sharp transition or a quenched statement. No overlap conclusion is asserted for the SK–Curie–Weiss model in Corollary <a href="#cor:skcw" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="cor:skcw">4</a>.

<a id="pm-h-8"></a>
#### Organization and order of limits

Sections <a href="#sec:foundations" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:foundations">2</a>–<a href="#sec:paths" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:paths">3</a> develop the finite-tree calculus and admissible comparison paths. The pair inverse in Section <a href="#sec:inverse" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:inverse">5</a> first supplies the global trial accuracy of Section <a href="#sec:global" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:global">6</a>; that accuracy and the local auxiliary comparisons give the genuine-path budgets of Section <a href="#sec:budgets" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:budgets">7</a>. The analytic inputs for the modified optimizers are proved within that section before their use. Section <a href="#sec:statistics" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:statistics">8</a> derives genuine-path statistics from the budgets and uses the pair inverse again in its high-mass covariance equation. Scalar compression in Section <a href="#sec:expansion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:expansion">9</a> and the common parameter order in Section <a href="#sec:parameters" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:parameters">10</a> complete Proposition <a href="#prop:increment" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:increment">15</a>. The conditional deduction in Section <a href="#sec:reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:reduction">4</a> then gives full-sequence moment convergence, positive limiting variance, moment determinacy, the finite-system law specification, and exact finite-size standardization. Section <a href="#sec:consequences" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:consequences">11</a> contains the proofs of the two corollaries stated above.

All conclusions are for a fixed $\beta>1$. Moment orders, expansion orders, and propagation depths are finite and fixed before $N\to\infty$. Their values may depend on the desired estimate. The exponent used for the small Laplace test is chosen only after the power saving in the increment estimate is established.

<a id="sec:foundations"></a>
### Hierarchical Gaussian calculus

The size comparison uses two kinds of calculation: expectations under hierarchical probability laws, and signed sums of such expectations produced by covariance differentiation. We define these separately. The resulting finite-order cavity and size expansions express pressure changes in terms of overlap errors relative to a one-site scalar model.

<a id="pm-h-10"></a>
#### Normalization and positive tree laws

We refer to (OpenAI 2026) <a id="pm-cite-28"></a>[[PE](#ref-PE)] as PE; references explicitly marked PE concern that paper. Fix $T=\beta^2>1$. As in <a href="#eq:completed-free-energy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:completed-free-energy">[eq:completed-free-energy]</a>, we add an independent spin-constant Gaussian of variance $T/2$ and use the uniform probability prior on spins. The resulting matrix covariance is $mTQ^2/2$, where $Q$ is the overlap defined below. The added Gaussian has bounded moments, and replacing the counting prior by the probability prior shifts only the mean.

We work in dyads $N\le m\lesssim 2N$ (with small enlargements), $m$ the integer number of sites, and put $x=N^{-1/6}$. All exponents below, including any order of a Taylor expansion, are fixed as $N\to\infty$; constants can depend on these choices and on $T$. We use “with subpower loss” or $\lesssim_\circ$ to allow $C_\epsilon x^{-\epsilon}$ for *every* sufficiently small fixed $\epsilon>0$. “Power small” means $O(x^c)$ for some fixed $c>0$; for assertions in every fixed $L^p$ a power saving not indexed by $p$ means the exponent is independent of the fixed finite moment order (constant and threshold need not be). Power slack choices in estimates with an indicated hierarchy of exponents are made before using subpower losses.

Estimates in this dyadic notation apply with $N/2\le m\le3N$; changing comparison scales by bounded factors from this convention is immaterial. Several pieces have local variables (including error majorants and truncation orders) redefined in each calculation. In particular the path martingale $X_v$ below is unrelated to the notation for the standardized free energy, and in Section <a href="#sec:budgets" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:budgets">7</a> the letter $X$ without a path subscript is also used for a scale ratio.

Fix a terminal mass $a\in[1,4]$. The coordinate $v\in(0,a)$ is the replica mass, and the deterministic nonnegative nondecreasing functions $b,h$ are the matrix and spin-field clocks. Jumps are allowed. Their cumulative Gaussian covariance at mass $v$ is $$m(b(v)Q^2/2+h(v)Q),\qquad
 Q=m^{-1}\sum_{i\le m}\sigma_i\sigma'_i.$$ For step clocks, construct independent Gaussian increments with these covariance increases, including any initial increment at mass zero. If $H$ is their sum, the terminal continuation is $a^{-1}\log\int e^{aH}$, with the integral taken against the uniform probability prior. Compute earlier continuations backwards: for an increment at mass $v>0$, set $$F_{\rm before}=v^{-1}\log\mathbf E\exp(vF_{\rm after}),$$ where this expectation averages only that increment. At mass zero use ordinary expectation. Divide the resulting deterministic value by $m$ and subtract $a(b(a-)/4+h(a-)/2)$; this defines the self-corrected pressure $f_m(b,h)$. Its interval length $a$ will be implicit.

The same continuations define a forward probability law. Reveal each Gaussian increment with its original Gaussian density multiplied by $\exp(v(F_{\rm after}-F_{\rm before}))$, and then draw the terminal spin from the Gibbs law of exponent $a$. The backward recursion makes each transition integrate to one. On a fixed finite rooted tree, branches share the increments before their fork and use conditionally independent forward transitions afterwards. We call this the *positive tree law* and write $\nu[P]$ for its expectation of $P$, including both fields and terminal spins. The tree topology and clocks are fixed in this expectation. Bounded monotone clocks are obtained by the fixed-site step limits from PE stated below.

A specified observation may lie on either side of a jump or at an intermediate clock value. At a simultaneous jump we use the joint filling $$(b_t,h_t)=(b_-,h_-)+t(\Delta b,\Delta h),\qquad 0\le t\le1,$$ with mass held fixed, and preserve this filling in step approximations. Endpoint tree laws and mass-integrated identities do not depend on the order of revelation within a same-mass jump. The separate matrix and field contributions to quadratic variation, and observations at intermediate cuts, do use the prescribed filling.

For a single path let $y=\sigma/\sqrt m$, $$\begin{gathered}
 X_v=\mathbf E_v y,\qquad C_v=\mathbf E_v(y-X_v)(y-X_v)^{\mathsf T},\\
 S_v=\mathbf E|X_v|^2,\qquad
 B_v=\mathbf E\|\mathbf E_v yy^{\mathsf T}\|_{\rm HS}^2,\qquad D_v^2=B_v-S_v^2.
\end{gathered}$$ Here $\mathbf E_v$ is conditional expectation given the fields revealed through the specified cut, and $\mathbf E$ averages the full single-path positive law. Thus $X_v,C_v$ are functions of the random prefix, whereas $S_v,B_v,D_v$ are deterministic statistics of that law. Write $H_v$ for the Hessian of the continuation with respect to a source coupled to $y$ in the downstream Hamiltonian, with the revealed prefix held fixed. Put $L_v=y\cdot X_v-|X_v|^2/2$ and $W_v=(y-X_v)^{\mathsf T}H_v(y-X_v)$. These last two observables also retain the terminal spin.

<a id="pm-h-11"></a>
#### Pinned moments and projection

The next estimates distinguish a variation of the deterministic clocks from movement along one fixed revealed path. In the pressure formula, $db(v),dh(v)$ are clock variations in an external parameter. In the susceptibility inequality, $dS_v$ and $dh$ are instead Stieltjes increments along the fixed path, including its prescribed filling at a jump. The source Hessian $H_v$ always keeps the revealed prefix fixed.

<a id="stmt-found-estimates"></a>
<div id="found:estimates" class="lemma">

<a id="eq:A1"></a>
<a id="eq:A2"></a>
**Lemma 6** (Pressure, source, and single-path estimates). *For the positive laws just defined, the following identities and inequalities hold at every fixed size. The moment bounds in <a href="#eq:A1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A1">[eq:A1]</a>–<a href="#eq:A2" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A2">[eq:A2]</a> hold for every fixed real $2\le p<\infty$, with deterministic $k\in L^2(0,a)$ and zero deterministic external field. $$\begin{split}
 df_m&=-\tfrac14\int B_v\,db(v)\,dv-\tfrac12\int S_v\,dh(v)\,dv,\\
 vC_v\preceq H_v\preceq a C_v,\qquad
 d S_v&\ge m\,\mathbf E\operatorname{tr}H_v^2\,dh,\qquad
 \mathbf EW_v=\mathbf E\operatorname{tr}C_v H_v,\\
 \left\|\int k_v(L_v-\mathbf EL_v)dv\right\|_p^2&\le c_p\left\|\int k_v^2 W_v\,dv\right\|_{p/2}.
\end{split}                                                    \tag{A1}\label{eq:A1}$$ The last line is a moment estimate under the full single-path law, with deterministic weights $k_v$ and zero deterministic external field. More generally, for polynomials $P_v$ of fixed degree with bounded deterministic coefficients, $$\left\|\int k_v(P_v(L_v)-\mathbf E P_v(L_v))dv\right\|_p^2
 \le c_p\left\|\int k_v^2 P'_v(L_v)^2 W_v\,dv\right\|_{p/2}.
                                                               \tag{A2}\label{eq:A2}$$*

<a id="eq:A3"></a>
*For the projection bound only, assume that the total clocks are at most a fixed power of $\log N$, and that the positive mass and field length are bounded below by inverse powers of $N$. If a branch has traversed a pure or mixed clock interval with field length $\Delta h>0$ after separating from the data determining an anchor vector $V$, and its mass is at least $v>0$ throughout that interval, then for every fixed even $p\ge2$, $$\|V\cdot(y-X_{\rm end})\|_p
 \lesssim_p \frac{\log^2 N}{v\sqrt{m\Delta h}}\,\|V\|_p                       \tag{A3}\label{eq:A3}$$*

*where the vector norm inside $L^p$ is Euclidean. The branch must retain its normalized future kernel conditional on the prefix and outside data; in particular, the bound applies to conditionally independent resamplings.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-found-estimates"><summary>Proof of stmt-found-estimates</summary>

*Proof.* Equations <a href="#eq:A1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A1">[eq:A1]</a> and <a href="#eq:A3" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A3">[eq:A3]</a> are the pressure, source, pinned-moment, and projection estimates of (OpenAI 2026, Lemmas 2.1–2.3 and 3.5, equations (1) and (13)) <a id="pm-cite-29"></a>[[PE](#ref-PE)]. To match the terminal-mass-one normalization there, put $$u=v/a,\qquad \widetilde b(u)=a^2b(au),\qquad
 \widetilde h(u)=a^2h(au),\qquad \widetilde F=aF.$$ The conditional spin means and covariances are unchanged, while $H_{au}=a\widetilde H_u$. The projection denominator is unchanged as well, since $(v/a)\sqrt{m a^2\Delta h}=v\sqrt{m\Delta h}$. Appendix <a href="#sec:companion-interface" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:companion-interface">12</a> records the pressure and moment conversions. The fixed-size path-limit result is PE, Proposition 2.14.

For <a href="#eq:A2" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A2">[eq:A2]</a>, we include the polynomial argument of PE, Appendix, paragraph “Source and pressure calculus; the scope of pinned moments.” Pin the terminal spin and write the Gaussian increments in terms of standard Gaussian drivers, as in the proof of PE, Lemma 2.3. Let $\mathsf A_v$ be the Hessian of the continuation in these drivers and $\mathsf B_v$ its mixed Hessian with the normalized spin source. After the transition densities telescope, the negative logarithm of the pinned driver density is the Gaussian quadratic potential minus $aH_\sigma$, which is linear, plus $\int_0^a F_v\,dv$, where $F_v$ is the continuation at the cut $v$. Consequently $$\begin{pmatrix}\mathsf A_v&\mathsf B_v\\
 \mathsf B_v^{\mathsf T}&H_v\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
 \qquad
 \mathsf Q=I+\int_0^a\mathsf A_v\,dv,$$ where $\mathsf Q$ is the Hessian of the negative logarithm of the pinned driver density. The driver gradient of $L_v$ is $g_v=\mathsf B_v(y-X_v)$. Thus, for every driver direction $z$, $|z\cdot g_v|^2\le(z^{\mathsf T}\mathsf A_vz)W_v$. For the polynomial observable set $$G_P=\int_0^a k_vP'_v(L_v)g_v\,dv,
 \qquad R_P=\int_0^a k_v^2P'_v(L_v)^2W_v\,dv.$$ Cauchy–Schwarz in $v$ gives $|z\cdot G_P|^2\le(z^{\mathsf T}\mathsf Qz)R_P$, hence $G_P^{\mathsf T}\mathsf Q^{-1}G_P\le R_P$. The inverse-Hessian Brascamp–Lieb inequality (Brascamp and Lieb 1976, Theorem 4.1) <a id="pm-cite-30"></a>[[BL1976](#ref-BL1976)] therefore gives <a href="#eq:A2" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A2">[eq:A2]</a> for $p=2$. Applying the same variance inequality to the $p/2$-th absolute power of the centered integral, as in PE, Lemma 2.3, gives the assertion for every fixed $p>2$.

The zero-field spin gauge transformations act transitively on terminal spins and preserve both $L_v$ and $W_v$. Because the coefficients of $P_v$ and the weights $k_v$ are deterministic, they also preserve the polynomial integral and $R_P$. Their conditional laws are consequently independent of the pinned spin, including the mean used for centering. Averaging over that spin yields the full single-path estimate. Bounded-weight approximation and then the fixed-$m$ path limit give the stated range of clocks and weights.

Clocks are bounded for each $N$, possibly by a power of $\log N$; <a href="#eq:A1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A1">[eq:A1]</a> is clock independent. For <a href="#eq:A3" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A3">[eq:A3]</a>, we apply PE, equation (13), only in this bounded or polylogarithmic clock regime; together with the polynomial mass and field-length bounds, this gives the polynomial coefficient-ratio bounds needed in its moment iteration, as detailed in Appendix <a href="#sec:companion-interface" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:companion-interface">12</a>. Our estimates can always be passed from affine finite-step interpolations, or from inserted fixed cuts, by the fixed-$m$ limit assertion, keeping chosen revelation sides and the joint filling at observed intermediate jump cuts, and using the corresponding integrated inequalities. In particular no discretization *rate* in $m$ is used.

The pinned inequalities in this lemma concern the full single-path law. When a tree contains additional branches, we first marginalize the branches not used by the test. Random factors retained on other branches are subsequently handled by unconditional Hölder inequalities; they are not made into random weights in <a href="#eq:A2" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:A2">[eq:A2]</a>. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-12"></a>
#### Signed allocation of replica labels

Covariance derivatives introduce additional replica labels. For a simple example, start with one observed leaf above a cut $v$, and divide its edge at a level $u\in(v,a)$. An extra label may coincide with that leaf, with coefficient $a$, or split from it along either edge interval, with coefficient minus the interval length. On a constant summand the total is $a-(a-u)-(u-v)=v$. In a larger tree, attachment to a fork also contributes an atom. We sum all these placements by the signed rule of PE, Section 2, Proposition 2.5, equation (2), and Lemmas 2.6, 2.8, and 2.9. A new label coinciding with an observed leaf has coefficient $a$; a new split on an occupied edge has coefficient $-dv$; attachment at an existing mass-$v$ fork with $d$ children has coefficient $-(d-1)v$. These coefficients multiply expectations under the positive laws just defined. They are not probabilities.

The row-sum rule sums one free label whose summand is constant over all its attachments in a block above a cut $v$. The result is that constant times $v$, as in the example. A row whose summand depends on its attachment cannot be collapsed this way. Empty levels can be inserted continuously without changing the calculation.
